The assistant should not be defined by hidden neural weights or by a large memoized answer table. It should be defined by an inspectable associative network of links: user messages, source data, inferred meanings, commands, test results, generated code, failures, permissions, and final answers.\n\nThe associative network is the AI. The runtime should activate, extend, query, and simplify that network as work happens.\n\nThe fact-checked design theses behind “AI = data + algorithm,” “everything is a\nlink,” transformation networks, controlled self-modification, recursive\ndecomposition, and Markov substitution are in\n[`docs/philosophy.md`](docs/philosophy.md). That guide distinguishes metaphor,\nmathematical fact, implemented behavior, and target behavior.\n\nThis places Formal AI squarely in the tradition of [symbolic artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbolic_artificial_intelligence) (GOFAI): the link network is a [semantic network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semantic_network) in the classical sense, and intelligence is the rule-driven manipulation of human-readable symbols ([physical symbol system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_symbol_system) hypothesis, Newell & Simon 1976) rather than numeric optimization of hidden weights. The audit in [`docs/case-studies/issue-451/symbolic-ai-best-practices.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-451/symbolic-ai-best-practices.md) maps each of the field's best practices onto this associative stack.\n\n## Who This Is For And What Pain It Closes\n\nBefore the architecture, the people. Mainstream AI assistants share a cluster of\npains: you cannot see *why* an answer was produced, the same prompt is not\nguaranteed to return the same answer, useful answers require a GPU and a vendor's\ncloud, the assistant's memory is an opaque store you cannot export or move, and\nyou cannot teach it by editing data instead of retraining weights.\n\nFormal AI is for the person who needs the opposite of each: a **defensible,\nreproducible, ownable, editable** answer. The auditor who must cite reasoning,\nthe multilingual user who wants `en | ru | hi | zh` treated equally, the learner\nwho wants honest execution notes on generated code, the analyst who needs math\nand currency with shown work, the integrator who wants a drop-in\nOpenAI-compatible endpoint with no GPU bill, the privacy-conscious owner who\nexports everything the agent saw and did as one file, and the tinkerer who\nreconfigures behavior by editing seed data.\n\nA concrete example user journey — Dana the auditor asks `What is 8% of $50?`,\ngets `$4`, then asks `Why did you answer that?` and receives the recorded\nimpulse, formalization, decomposition, validation, and simplification that\nproduced it — is walked end to end in\n[`docs/USER-JOURNEYS.md`](docs/USER-JOURNEYS.md). That document enumerates\n**every user journey supported today and every journey we could support next**,\nmapped to the surfaces below and to the principles in this file, so the vision\nmakes a concrete promise rather than only describing the machine.\n\n## Core Idea\n\nThe system should prefer deep understanding of user needs, intent, context, and available evidence over answer memoization. A prompt should trigger enough data collection and reasoning to justify the response for that prompt. What the system learns along the way should remain available as reviewable knowledge, with source links and execution traces attached.\n\nThe default native store is link-native:\n\n- The `link-cli` library is the default native Links Data Store boundary for meanings, history, rules, traces, and executable associations, using its transactional file-mapped `doublets-rs` backend.\n- `doublets-web` / IndexedDB is the browser-side storage shape.\n- Links Notation is the reviewable text format for seed data, portable packages, traces, and repository data.\n- Doublet links are the primitive storage model for this project.\n- `lino-objects-codec` remains useful for converting structured objects into reviewable Links Notation during the transition.\n\nThe dynamic type system should be expressible with doublets:\n\n```text\nType -> SubType\nSubType -> SubType\nSubType -> Value\n```\n\nThis keeps the seed model small while letting the network define new concepts, instances, relations, handlers, and rules as they are needed.\n\n## Operating Principles\n\n- Small seeds, dynamic growth: start with the smallest useful seed dataset, then construct missing knowledge on demand.\n- Transparent reasoning: every step, decision, command, data access, and answer should be traceable to links and source events.\n- Add-only history: changes requested by users or made by the assistant should be appended as events first, then projected into the current state.\n- User-queryable memory: the user should be able to ask about any relevant detail in the associative network and receive a traceable answer.\n- Chat-first interface: chat should be the default interface for English, Russian, Hindi, Chinese, and later other languages.\n- Visual network on demand: the link graph should be available side by side with chat when the user wants deeper inspection.\n- Bounded chat autonomy: chat mode should do only enough work to answer the current message, including compiling or running code when appropriate.\n- Explicit agent autonomy: agent mode should expose actions and run them in an isolated environment such as a Docker image, a server sandbox, or a browser VM where practical.\n\n## Reasoning Model\n\nThe assistant should use a universal problem-solving loop:\n\n1. Record the user message as an impulse event.\n2. Identify unknown concepts, requirements, constraints, and missing context.\n3. Search local links first, then external sources if local data is insufficient.\n4. Convert findings into link-native meanings with source metadata.\n5. Split the problem into smaller tasks until each task is executable or answerable.\n6. Draft experiments together with tests and traces.\n7. Select a passing draft, execute it where permitted, and compose its result.\n8. On failure, shrink to smaller tasks; at an unsupported leaf, extend the tool,\n   retry the leaf, then climb back up and retest the whole task.\n9. Record results, failures, and learned procedures.\n10. Return the smallest sufficient answer plus links to the relevant trace.\n\nThis loop can be implemented first as ordinary Rust logic, then increasingly represented as link substitutions, triggers, and reusable associative packages.\n\n## Universal Problem-Solving Algorithm\n\nThe reasoning loop above is the outer skeleton. The inner mechanics should be a single universal algorithm that does not assume prior knowledge of the task and works in the same shape for greetings, code generation, translation, source-checking, agent actions, or any future request:\n\n1. **Impulse**: append the raw user message as an `impulse` event in the append-only log.\n2. **Formalization**: turn the impulse into a `requirement` record. The algorithm decides — controlled by a configurable knob — whether to guess the formalization from context or to ask the user the smallest possible clarifying question.\n3. **Context and domain data**: derive the language, surface, mode flags (chat vs agent, diagnostic on/off), and the domain (greeting, code, translation, math, agent action) from the formalized requirement.\n4. **History lookup**: check whether the same or a similar requirement has been solved before; if so, reuse the prior solution and record a `cache_hit` link.\n5. **Decomposition**: when the requirement is composite (multiple clauses, \"and\", \"with tests\", \"with benchmarks\"), split it into sub-impulses and recursively formalize each one until every sub-requirement is small enough to be solved directly.\n6. **TDD-style test generation**: derive at least one executable check or assertion that any candidate solution must pass.\n7. **Draft experiments and selection**: build testable drafts by (a) reusing known parts, (b) reasoning from rules, and (c) random or evolutionary search where structure and compute budget allow; select only a test-passing draft and record why it won.\n8. **Composition**: combine selected partial solutions back into a full solution that addresses the original requirement.\n9. **Verification and recursive recovery**: run the composed solution against the whole-task test. On failure, record `trace:execution_failure`, descend to smaller tasks, and retry upward after their tests pass. At an elementary task with no method, extend the general tool and retry that leaf. Bounds on depth and retries keep this executable loop finite.\n10. **Simplification**: apply transformation rules that preserve meaning to shorten the answer and the reasoning trace. Pick the smallest sufficient form.\n11. **Documentation and presentation**: produce the user-facing reply, the Links Notation trace, and the visible evidence links. If the user asks for execution, run the code in the appropriate isolation level.\n\nEvery step writes its own event to the append-only log so the user can ask the chat why the assistant did what it did and get a traceable answer from the recorded experience.\n\n## Configurable Solver Knobs\n\nThe universal algorithm should be controlled by a small, explicit, persistable `SolverConfig` so the same engine can be tuned per surface or per user:\n\n- `guess_probability` — how often the algorithm guesses a formalization vs. asking a clarifying question (`0.0` = always ask, `1.0` = always guess).\n- `context_sensitivity` — how aggressively the algorithm uses surrounding context (previous messages, recent events) when formalizing.\n- `questioning_rigor` — how strict the clarifying questions are (`0.0` = accept almost anything, `1.0` = ask until the requirement is fully formal).\n- `max_decomposition_depth` — how deep the recursive decomposition is allowed to go.\n- `agent_mode` — whether agent mode is opted in. Off by default.\n- `diagnostic_mode` — whether diagnostic links are echoed in the user-facing reply.\n- `offline` — whether external lookups are allowed (also honored from the `FORMAL_AI_OFFLINE` environment variable).\n- `cache_ttl_seconds` — TTL for cached external sources (default ≈ two months).\n- `temperature` — controls how aggressively the formalization step collapses multiple candidate interpretations into one. Lower values bias the solver toward the highest-scoring interpretation; higher values keep more interpretations alive and trigger clarifying questions or guesses, depending on `guess_probability`. Modelled on the softmax-temperature pattern used by neural networks, but applied to discrete Wikidata-anchored interpretations and symbolic probability evidence rather than neural logits.\n\nThese knobs are deterministic: the same prompt with the same config produces the same answer. \"Random guessing\" is seeded from the impulse content hash so reproducibility is preserved.\n\n## Formalization And Temperature\n\nThe reasoning loop is built around an explicit formalization layer rather than memoized prompt → answer pairs. Every input message is first translated into Links Notation as a sequence of statements or questions and appended to memory in its original form. The translated statement is then formalized: each verb phrase is mapped to a Wikidata **P-id** (property), each noun phrase to a Wikidata **Q-id** (item), with a fallback chain to Wikipedia article links and Wiktionary entries when no Wikidata anchor exists. A candidate formalization is only accepted when the targeted concept actually mentions the surface form and matches it semantically — otherwise the candidate is recorded as `formalization_unresolved` and the next candidate is tried.\n\nMultiple plausible formalizations are scored, then a temperature-controlled selector picks among them in the same way neural networks pick among logits: lower temperature collapses onto the highest-scoring interpretation; higher temperature keeps competing interpretations alive. When two or more candidates have probabilities that are equal or close, the solver either asks the smallest clarifying question that distinguishes them or guesses according to `guess_probability` — the choice is config-driven and visible in the trace. Every interpretation, every clarifying question, every guess, every accepted formalization, and every fallback is appended to the event log so the user can ask \"why did you read it that way?\" and get a complete answer.\n\nProbability evidence must remain part of the same symbolic network. Bayesian-style evidence records and Markov-style transition records are Links Notation data with provenance, timestamps, cached-source fingerprints, and deterministic replay. They can bias candidate formalizations or answer candidates, but they never modify neural weights and never call neural inference; they only adjust symbolic posterior scores before the existing temperature and clarify-vs-guess policy runs.\n\nThe full pipeline is documented in [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md).\n\n## Growable Memory And Public Knowledge As Cache\n\nMemory should grow with use, not just with prompts. Every reasoning step, every internal decision, every external request, and every response is appended to the same log so the next similar request can reuse the prior work in part or in full. The default native store is link-cli's transactional file-mapped doublets store in the library, CLI, server, and Telegram surfaces, with doublets-web (IndexedDB / `localStorage`) on the browser; portable source and backup documents are written as `.lino` files representing Links Notation, both to disk and to additional persistent storage (browser IndexedDB, future cloud sync).\n\nTreating the internet (Wikipedia, Wikidata, Wiktionary, Wikifunctions, Rosetta Code, public APIs) as a public database and the local doublets store as a cache for that database substitutes deterministic reasoning over reviewable links for opaque GPU-backed inference. The same caching pattern carries `source:`, `fetched_at`, and `sha256` metadata per the existing `cache_ttl_seconds` policy; offline mode refuses external lookups and emits a `policy:offline` event instead of synthesizing facts.\n\n## Append-Only Event Log\n\nEvery action the algorithm takes is appended to an in-process event log before the answer is built. Each event carries a kind (`impulse`, `language_detected`, `local_search`, `external_search`, `sub_impulse`, `candidate`, `validation`, `policy`, `agent_action`, `cache_hit`, `source`, `trace`, `error`) and is identified by a content-addressed id. The event log is the system of record; the answer and the evidence links are projections of it. The user can chat over this log:\n\n- \"Why did you answer that?\" returns a meta-explanation built from the most recent trace.\n- \"What do you know about X?\" returns the links involving X.\n- \"List the facts I have contributed\" filters by user.\n- \"Forget X\" is refused unless the explicit retraction protocol is used, because the log is append-only.\n- \"Export the network\" returns the Links Notation snapshot of the seed dataset plus the visible event log.\n\n## Computation Model\n\nFormal AI should use trigger-style computation over links. A trigger can react to insertion, update, deletion, or a matched pattern in the network. Substitution rules should be first-class knowledge and should be able to express reads, writes, transformations, and simplification passes. The associative store supports five rule shapes, ranked from most reviewable to most flexible:\n\n1. **Pure data rules** — `when x do y` substitutions stored directly as doublets, executable by a simple matcher in any environment.\n2. **Compiled Rust handlers** — registered through `solver_handlers` and addressable as data so the rule index can point at them.\n3. **Compiled JS handlers** — registered through the browser worker and addressable the same way, so the same rule can have language-specific implementations; under the compiled-logic doctrine this shape is transitional — logic belongs in compiled Rust (native or WASM), and the JS registration surface remains only until the worker absorption (issue #658) completes.\n4. **Dynamically compiled Rust/JS code stored as data** — source text is itself a link payload; the runtime can compile-on-demand and cache the resulting handler.\n5. **Natural-language skills / instructions** — stored as `.lino` text, executed either by an interpreter that walks them one step at a time or by an on-demand compiler that translates them into rules in any of the four shapes above (and ultimately into native binaries when the platform allows).\n\nDeep.Foundation is a useful reference for associative packages, handlers, permissions, and code stored inside associative memory. This project adapts those ideas to local Rust, browser, and CLI modes using Link Foundation doublets instead of triplet links. `ARCHITECTURE.md` documents the data shape of each rule kind and how the trigger loop dispatches across them.\n\n## Product Shape\n\nThe same symbolic core should be available through:\n\n- Rust library API.\n- CLI chat and dataset commands.\n- OpenAI-compatible HTTP API surfaces.\n- Docker-ready microservice.\n- GitHub Pages chat demo backed by a Rust WebAssembly worker.\n- Telegram private and public chat surfaces.\n- Desktop and embedded agent modes share the same library boundary; the desktop wrapper is tracked by issue [#280](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/280).\n- VS Code extension (desktop and web/`vscode.dev`) embedding the same chat; Marketplace publication is tracked by issue [#666](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/666).\n- OpenAI-compatible backend for agentic CLIs (codex, opencode, gemini, qwen, claude, agent), and — the mirror direction — an orchestrator that drives those same CLIs as permissioned tools (issue [#703](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/703)).\n\nCode-generation tasks should be a first focus area. The assistant should generate algorithms in popular languages, compile or run generated code when the environment supports it, report execution limits honestly, and preserve logs for failed reasoning or failed execution. Browser-only mode can start with JavaScript evaluation and later experiment with WebVM.\n\n## Meaning And Identity\n\nFor every uniquely defined concept, the system should converge on one meaning link. If the same name points to two different meanings, the system should split them into separate concepts and record why. The network should remain dynamically growing and incomplete, but it should actively reduce contradictions as new evidence arrives.\n\nEvery meaning should be explainable through other meanings. Human-readable\nglosses and source labels are useful annotations, but the primary semantic\nstructure should be recursive links: `defined_by` links for ontology reduction\nand semantic facets for notation, annotation, denotation, and connotation. The\nfacet kinds themselves are meanings in the seed, so adding a new semantic view\nis data growth rather than a new hardcoded language constant.\n\nThe semantic root should also stay compatible with Links Theory: `reference`,\n`link_action`, defined connectives, quantity primitives, and self-equations are\nseed meanings, and ambiguous symbols are split into distinct meanings such as\n`bank_river` and `bank_money` instead of one overloaded surface.\n\nNatural languages and programming languages should be translated through link-native meanings rather than through one-off text rewrites. Once a phrase has been fully formalized — verbs mapped to Wikidata P-IDs, nouns mapped to Q-IDs, fallbacks documented to Wikipedia or Wiktionary entries — translating it to another language reduces to looking up the destination-language label on the same P/Q anchor. The same mechanism translates between natural language and programming languages: formalized statements can be rendered into Rust, JavaScript, or any other target whose syntactic forms have been linked into the doublet store. Links Notation acts as the intermediate language of meaning for explanations, code generation, data imports, cross-language translation, and on-demand compilation of natural-language skills into executable code.\n\nCross-language translation should also preserve the source's surface signal: the leading capitalization and the terminal punctuation a user typed are part of the meaning, not noise. A lowercase `как у тебя дела?` should round-trip to lowercase `how are you?`, and a source fragment with no terminal mark should not gain one in the target language. The pipeline is `formalize → meaning → deformalize → match_source_formatting`, and the meaning ID, source language, and target language remain in the Links Notation trace so the translation stays inspectable.\n\nIssue #526 makes round-trip survival the translation quality contract. Every\nsupported language must pass a language-to-meta-to-same-language check with no\ndata loss, and every supported language pair must translate through the shared\nmeaning before rendering a target surface. Direct pair-specific translation can\nonly be an implementation detail below that contract; it is not acceptable as a\nquality path when it bypasses the meta language. The same rule applies to code:\na Rust <-> JavaScript translation must preserve the code meaning link, not only\nproduce syntax that looks plausible.\n\n## Data Is The Interface\n\nThe shell code should be about *interfacing* (rendering chat, dispatching tools, persisting events) and not about *logic*. The agent's identity, its multilingual responses, its concept table, and its registered tools should all live in seeded Links Notation files inside an associative store, so a user can fully reconfigure the agent — add a new language, retire an answer, register a new tool, change a rule — by editing data, not by rewriting code. The same principle applies to executable knowledge: precompiled handlers can be seeded, and dynamically-compiled Rust, JavaScript, and WebAssembly snippets can be linked into the store on demand, so the data graph itself defines what the agent can do.\n\nConcretely, `data/seed/` is the canonical knowledge surface for every interface in this repository. The browser worker fetches the files at runtime through `src/web/seed_loader.js`; the Rust library, CLI binary, HTTP server, and Telegram webhook read the same files through `src/seed.rs`, which `include_str!`-embeds each `.lino` at compile time so even offline builds expose the same data. `scripts/sync-seed.sh` keeps `src/web/seed/` mirrored from `data/seed/` for the GitHub Pages deploy. The seed currently covers multilingual responses, the concept table, the tool registry (HTTP fetch, web search, Wikipedia lookup, JS execution, local file read, memory append, memory export — each tagged `thinking` or `agent`), language-detection rules, prompt-question patterns, identity metadata, greetings, hello-world programs, demo dialogs, and the **intent-routing rule book** (`keyword` / `phrase` / `token` / `combo` semantics) that decides which handler runs for a given prompt. Any environment-specific tool (axios, file I/O, bash, docker, container actions) is registered through the same data shape.\n\n## Single-File Reproducibility\n\nEvery interface should offer a one-click way to capture the full agent state — the seed, the modified data, the UI preferences, and the entire append-only memory log — as one Links Notation document, and every default-labelled export action should produce that **full** document. The web demo's **Export memory** topbar button writes `formal-ai-memory.lino` as a complete `formal_ai_bundle` (seed + events + preferences + environment metadata + version), so a single click is enough to reconstitute the session. The \"Report issue\" link instructs the user to wrap that same file in a `.zip` (GitHub's issue uploader does not yet accept `.lino`) and to redact sensitive content before attaching. On the Rust side, `seed::merged_bundle()` produces the equivalent `formal_ai_seed_bundle` document, `seed::parse_bundle()` (mirrored in JS by `FormalAiSeed.parseBundle` / `FormalAiSeed.loadFromBundle`) recovers the per-category split files from it, and `memory::export_full_memory` / `memory::import_full_memory` round-trip the full `formal_ai_bundle` including the embedded `demo_memory` log. The CLI matches: `formal-ai memory export` defaults to the full bundle (with `--events-only` opting back into the legacy `demo_memory` shape), `formal-ai memory import` / `formal-ai bundle import` auto-detect either format, and both print `Migration: <message>` notices when the imported seed version differs from the running app's. A user can always say \"here is everything my agent saw and did\" in a single file, regardless of which surface they were on.\n\n## Self-Aware Environments\n\nThe seed must describe every environment the agent can run in. `data/seed/environments.lino` (loaded as `seed::environment_directory` in Rust and `FormalAiSeed.extractEnvironmentDirectory` in the browser) lists each interface (`browser`, `rust_library`, `cli`, `http_server`, `telegram`, `docker_microservice`) along with the runtime that hosts it, the path it reads seed data from, where it persists memory, and the exact command to export/import that memory. The same file enumerates supported migration flows (browser ↔ CLI, browser ↔ browser, CLI ↔ CLI) and the Links Notation format that carries them. Running `formal-ai environments` prints this directory from the embedded seed, so the agent can answer \"where can you run?\" and \"how do I move your memory?\" from data instead of code.\n\n## Library-First Availability\n\nEvery capability the CLI or HTTP server exposes is also reachable from the `formal_ai` library crate root. Embedders writing their own surface (a desktop app, a bot for another platform, a research notebook) get the same `MemoryStore`, `MemoryEvent`, `export_memory_links_notation`, `parse_memory_links_notation`, `export_memory_bundle`, `extract_memory_from_bundle`, `seed_files`, `merged_bundle`, `parse_bundle`, `environment_directory`, `environment_records`, `agent_info`, `intent_routing`, `multilingual_responses`, `language_rules`, and `prompt_patterns` accessors that the bundled binaries rely on. The shell code is interface; the library is logic.\n\n## Current Direction\n\nThe current repository is a deterministic symbolic implementation. It already has deterministic rules, Links Notation seed files, OpenAI-shaped API responses, a static web demo, Telegram support, execution metadata for simple code examples, and case-study documentation. Every interface now reads its multilingual responses, concept table, tool registry, language-detection rules, prompt patterns, and intent-routing rule book from the shared `data/seed/` directory through `src/seed.rs` (Rust) and `src/web/seed_loader.js` (browser). Reasoning steps and tool invocations land in the append-only memory log on the web side; the merged seed bundle round-trips through one `formal_ai_seed_bundle` Links Notation file via `seed::merged_bundle()` / `seed::parse_bundle()`.\n\nThe next step is to keep the implemented surfaces small while moving more of the assistant's behavior into explicit links: requirements, source facts, traces, prompts, handlers, permissions, tests, and reusable problem-solving procedures. The CLI, server, and Telegram bot should expose the same bundle-export and simplified-issue-reporting actions the web demo offers while preserving the unified link-cli/doublets-web store and Links Notation migration surface across interfaces.\n\nThe foundation batches E1-E20, the reasoning batch E21-E27, the synthesis batch E28-E32, and the parity batch E33-E34 are merged (PRs #305-#311, #319-#323, #328-#329). Every user message is now formalized into a Links Notation intent before routing, unmatched prompts run a reasoning-under-unknowns loop instead of falling through to \"I can't answer that\", narrow per-language intents are collapsed into a parametric `write a program` intent, behavior can be expressed as substitution rules (`replace x y`, `when n do m`) over link CRUD, natural language can query memory / call APIs / execute code under the permission model, a bounded isolated agent runs allowlisted commands, and progress is measured against an imported industry benchmark slice (HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K, MATH, BIG-bench).\n\nThe synthesis step is now **general**: instead of resolving answers from seeded handlers, the universal 11-step loop **derives** them by composing decomposed sub-results over the links network. The benchmark suite makes this concrete — it grew to a 13-case slice and passes **13/13** with a `minimum_pass_count` ratchet: the solver writes the HumanEval/MBPP Python functions (synthesized from spec + tests, verified in the bounded agent workspace) and computes the GSM8K (`18`), MATH (`11`), and BIG-bench object-counting (`3`) answers, all **without per-case memorization** (each source carries a held-out paraphrased variant).\n\nThe **parity** gap surfaced by the issue [#244](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/244) PR feedback — \"all Rust and JavaScript logic are in sync\" and \"all languages are supported equally\" — is now **closed** by the merged parity batch (E33-E34): the text-manipulation handler triggers from a single shared, data-driven multilingual operation vocabulary (`data/seed/operation-vocabulary.lino`) so every operation is recognised equally in `en|ru|hi|zh`, and the JavaScript browser worker derives the same synthesis/numeric/program/text answers as the Rust core, pinned by the shared fixture `data/parity/cross-runtime-synthesis.json`. With E1-E34 all merged, no vision-planning epic remains open for issue #244. See [`ROADMAP.md`](ROADMAP.md) for the gap-by-gap record.\n\nThe issue [#349](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/349)\nreverse-sort roadmap is also closed: issues #355-#364 implemented the\nreproduction, rule-synthesis design, active-program coreference, composable\nprogram modifiers, rule construction for unknown program follow-ups, default-off\ndiagnostics, Rust/browser-worker parity, a multilingual coding-modification\nratchet, reasoning-first report behavior, and the white-box self-improvement\nloop. The final epic #365 records that the original Russian dialog now produces\na `write_program` answer with reverse-sorted output instead of `unknown`, and\nthat the behavior is covered across runtime and benchmark surfaces.\n\nSince then the meta-algorithm layer has grown four self-directed capabilities,\neach delivered as a grounded recipe pinned to the live source\n(see [`docs/meta-algorithm.md`](docs/meta-algorithm.md)): the recursive meta\ncore with a live method registry and proposal-only self-improvement (issue\n[#559](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/559)), background\n**dreaming** that learns topics and requirements from memory and generalizes\nthem into meta-algorithm amendments (issue\n[#540](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/540)), the human-gated\n**self-healing** repair loop over the system's own source (issue\n[#558](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/558)), and the\n**agentic-coding** mode that lets external agent CLIs drive the same\ndeterministic loop through the OpenAI-compatible server (issues\n[#468](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/468),\n[#680](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/680)). The symbolic\n**world models** design — current-state and target-state contexts as links\nnetworks, their difference, merge/split, and action-consequence prediction — is\nspecified in [`docs/case-studies/issue-649`](docs/case-studies/issue-649/README.md)\nwith implementation tracked by issue\n[#702](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/702).\n\nThe self-evolution frontier is explicit and benchmark-gated: proposals must\npass tests and benchmark ratchets before a reviewed promotion materializes them\nas seed edits (issues [#656](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/656),\n[#701](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/701)); the share of\neach release authored by Formal AI itself is measured honestly from 0% upward\n(issue [#657](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/657)); the\nsolver should try multiple candidate drafts in parallel and record why the\nwinner won (issue [#704](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/704),\nfollowing the drafts→selection→composition shape of\n[konard/problem-solving](https://github.com/konard/problem-solving)); and the\nmeta-algorithm should predict the user's likely next requests per topic and\npre-learn them while idle (issue\n[#705](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/705)). Language\nbreadth grows by data alone through the meta language (issue\n[#706](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/706)), and computer-use\ntasks are handled as verified algorithmic plans over files, shell, and\nstructured web — no vision required at this stage (issue\n[#707](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/707)).\n\nThe executable recursive controller and the first live learning back-edge now\nexist: failed branches descend through an explicit task tree and retry upward;\nverified unknown-path events exported by the conversation API enter the normal\nrule learner; and an exact repeated failure consults a human-approved ledger\nlesson before deriving a new rule. This is a bounded first slice, not a claim\nthat the entire external-CLI orchestrator or autonomous self-coding loop is\ncomplete.\n\nIssue [#408](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/408) extends\nthe same deterministic path to user-requested text and code edits: follow-up\nreplacement requests can target the previous assistant artifact, including a\ngenerated code block, and the supported edit operations use the shared\nmultilingual operation vocabulary. The benchmark claim is manifest-backed:\nPR #416 lists 48 researched sources in\n`data/benchmarks/text-manipulation-suite.lino`, generates 30 deterministic local\nedit variations per source, and requires every source to pass both the explicit\n3-check repository-local 10% floor and the stronger 30/30 ratchet, for 1,440 of\n1,440 passing checks before the branch is complete.\n# Goals\n\nThis project should build a practical, inspectable symbolic assistant before it grows into a larger associative intelligence system.\n\n## Architecture Goals\n\n- Maintain the smallest useful seed dataset, then learn or import missing knowledge on demand.\n- Store meanings, events, traces, requirements, handlers, and answer evidence in a link-native form.\n- Use doublet links and Links Notation as the preferred representation for reviewable knowledge.\n- Keep the dynamic type system small enough to understand and flexible enough to grow.\n- Make transparent reasoning a default property of the system, not a diagnostics afterthought.\n- Preserve add-only history for user messages, assistant actions, external data accesses, edits, and state projections.\n- Support reusable associative packages for datasets, skills, substitution rules, and executable handlers.\n- Keep JavaScript as interfacing glue and JSX UI only; compile all logic from Rust (native on servers, WebAssembly in the web app) and reuse the same WASM engine across desktop and editor surfaces.\n\n## Product Goals\n\n- Keep chat-first interaction as the default user experience.\n- Support both ordinary chat mode and explicit agent mode.\n- Keep all public interfaces backed by the same symbolic core: Rust library, CLI, HTTP API, Docker service, GitHub Pages demo, Telegram, and future desktop mode.\n- Provide clear feedback when generated code was compiled, run, not run, or cannot be run in the current environment.\n- Support isolated execution for generated code and agent actions through Docker, server sandboxes, or browser-local VM technology where practical.\n- Let users inspect relevant links visually when chat is not enough.\n- Let users report, correct, add, update, and delete knowledge through natural language while preserving history.\n\n## Reasoning Goals\n\n- Convert each user message into traceable requirements, source events, and candidate meanings.\n- Search local associative knowledge first and external sources only when local knowledge is insufficient.\n- Cache external source access with provenance and refresh policy rather than treating the web as untracked context.\n- Split hard tasks recursively into smaller tasks that can be tested, executed, or answered.\n- Learn from failed code generation, failed tests, timeouts, and review comments.\n- Translate between natural languages, programming languages, and Links Notation as a language of meaning.\n- Reduce contradictions by splitting overloaded names into distinct meanings when needed.\n\n## Universal Solver Goals\n\n- Run the same universal problem-solving algorithm for every request: greetings, identity questions, code generation, translation, source checking, math, and agent actions. The shape of the loop should not branch by domain.\n- Treat formalization, decomposition, candidate generation, validation, and simplification as first-class steps that always run, even when the answer is trivially known.\n- Generate at least one executable test or constraint check per requirement before committing to an answer, following test-driven development.\n- Reuse known parts of prior solutions before generating new ones; record reuse as `cache_hit:` evidence with a link back to the prior trace.\n- When no reusable part exists, combine reasoning, random search, and evolutionary search according to the available compute budget instead of giving up.\n- After verification, apply meaning-preserving transformation rules to shorten the answer and pick the smallest sufficient form.\n- Surface execution failures as `trace:execution_failure` links instead of retrying silently.\n\n## Configurable Solver Goals\n\n- Expose every solver behavior through a small `SolverConfig` so the same engine can be tuned per surface or per user.\n- Make formalization preference configurable: how often to guess the formalization vs. ask the smallest clarifying question.\n- Make context sensitivity configurable: how aggressively earlier messages and recent events influence the current formalization.\n- Make questioning rigor configurable: how strict clarifying questions are before accepting a requirement as formal.\n- Make decomposition depth configurable so the loop does not spin forever on unsolvable problems.\n- Make agent mode opt-in by configuration, off by default, and only active in environments that declare isolation.\n- Make diagnostic visibility, offline mode, and source cache TTL configurable from environment variables and CLI flags.\n- Keep the algorithm deterministic for a given config: \"random guessing\" must be seeded from the impulse content hash so the same prompt produces the same answer.\n\n## Append-Only Event Log Goals\n\n- Record every step of the universal solver as an append-only event in the in-process log before the answer is built.\n- Tag each event with a stable, content-addressed id so users can reference and inspect it from chat.\n- Treat the user-facing answer as a projection of the event log, not the system of record.\n- Let users chat over the log: \"why did you answer that?\", \"what do you know about X?\", \"list facts I have contributed\", and \"export the network\" should all be answerable from the log.\n- Refuse \"forget X\" requests by default; require an explicit retraction protocol that itself appends a `retraction` event.\n- Tolerate concurrent reasoning steps by guaranteeing that the projected prefix never shrinks.\n\n## Chat-Over-Experience Goals\n\n- Make the recorded experience the assistant's memory: any link in the network should be addressable from chat by id or natural-language description.\n- Allow users to query reasoning by step: \"what was step 4 of your last answer?\" must return the corresponding event.\n- Allow users to query reasoning by domain: \"show me every external source you fetched today\" must filter the event log.\n- Allow users to contribute facts that become first-class events with the user as the source, attributable for later review.\n- Keep diagnostic output off by default; require an explicit opt-in flag or message prefix before flooding the chat with internal links.\n\n## World-Model Goals\n\n- Maintain a current-state context and a target-state context as links networks throughout every dialogue, and expose their difference on request.\n- Keep the user and the agent synchronized on the target state through an explicit, append-only confirmation loop.\n- Support merging and splitting context models, where every context is a links network — never embeddings.\n- Treat statements as dependent under relative-meta-logic: any change recalculates the probabilities of dependent statements, visibly.\n- Predict the consequences of a candidate action as a hypothetical context before executing it, and compare that context against the target state.\n- Persist meta-language expressions with usage (read) and change (write) counting derived from incoming and outgoing links, so frequently used or changed knowledge persists longer.\n\n## Agent Orchestration Goals\n\nThese are target capabilities. The current implementation serves the six\nregistered Agent CLIs and explicitly granted custom CLI/TUI or Bash adapters,\ndispatches bounded decompositions, compares parallel candidates, composes\npassing effects, resumes a disproved result in its exact native session, and\nproduces evidence-linked synthesis and learning proposals. Autonomous\npromotion remains human-gated, and cross-agent agreement is not a substitute\nfor primary-source fact verification.\n\n- Serve as an OpenAI-compatible backend that any agentic CLI (codex, opencode, gemini, qwen, claude, agent) can drive, with tools selected by formalized intent rather than phrasing.\n- Act as an orchestrator that drives those same agent CLIs as permissioned, isolated tools: dispatch decomposed sub-tasks, capture full sessions as append-only evidence, and verify results with generated tests.\n- Dispatch the same sub-task to multiple agents in parallel when configured, compare the verified results in a recorded ledger, and select the winner deterministically.\n- Complete the self-coding chain: Formal AI codes itself via Agent CLI, directed by Hive Mind, with every change landing as a reviewed pull request.\n- Keep every UI action, setting, and capability reachable through natural language in every environment, including agentic mode where no Formal AI UI exists.\n\n## Self-Evolution Goals\n\nThese are ratcheted targets, not assertions of present autonomy. Report upload\ncurrently stages verified traces for review, and approved exact lessons can be\nrecalled live; promotion remains explicitly benchmark- and human-gated.\n\n- Grow capabilities through a closed learning loop: frontier detection (unknown intents, failed benchmarks, trending questions) → candidate knowledge/rules with generated tests → benchmark-gated promotion as reviewed seed edits — never silent self-modification.\n- Prove every adopted item with a before/after capability pair, including held-out paraphrases, so learning is generalization rather than memorization.\n- Predict likely next user requests per topic from symbolic transition records and pre-learn what they need while idle, under the existing consent and priority rules.\n- Generate multiple independent candidate drafts per hard task, select by test oracle with a least-action tie-break, and record why the winner won.\n- Measure the share of each release authored by Formal AI itself, starting honestly at 0% and ratcheting upward.\n\n## Documentation Goals\n\n- Keep issue requirements in `REQUIREMENTS.md` (alongside `VISION.md`, `GOALS.md`, `NON-GOALS.md` at the repository root).\n- Keep deep issue analyses in `docs/case-studies/issue-{id}`.\n- Preserve raw GitHub data and relevant logs beside each case study.\n- Use case studies to explain root causes, alternatives, implementation choices, and follow-up boundaries.\n- Keep vision, goals, and non-goals explicit so future PRs can decide scope consistently.\n\n## Near-Term Goals\n\n- Expand the link-native dataset from current greetings, identity, demo dialogs, and hello-world examples into richer requirement, trace, and source records.\n- Introduce first-class trace links for commands, outputs, failures, and generated answers.\n- Implement a local link-store-backed reasoning loop that can read and write the same knowledge used by CLI, API, web, and Telegram surfaces.\n- Add a network visualization mode that starts from the links most relevant to the current dialog.\n- Keep every new behavior covered by focused unit, integration, or e2e tests before expanding scope.\n- Implement the universal solver and append-only event log inside the existing Rust engine so every chat answer surfaces the full evidence-link namespace expected by the full-scope test suite.\n- Promote knobs from `SolverConfig` to environment variables and CLI flags so the same engine can be operated in chat, agent, and offline modes without code changes.\n- Cover each step of the universal solver with explicit unit tests, including the failing tracked requirement tests under `tests/unit/specification/`, and graduate them out of `#[ignore]` as the implementation lands.\n# Non-Goals\n\nThese boundaries keep the project aligned with the symbolic, link-native direction.\n\n## Runtime Non-Goals\n\n- GPU-required neural inference is not a project target. The only sanctioned exception is the experimental, strictly opt-in small-model formalization fallback of issue [#483](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/483): off by default, never loaded unless requested, downloaded on demand, limited to choosing among symbolically generated options that unit tests confirm — LLMs are never in control, never at the steering wheel.\n- A memoized answer cache is not a substitute for reasoning from source data and traceable steps.\n- Hidden autonomous actions are not acceptable in chat mode.\n- Unbounded reasoning loops are not acceptable; long-running agent work must expose actions and logs.\n- Unverified generated code should not be presented as tested.\n- Silent execution failures should not be hidden from users.\n- Browser-only mode should not claim host-level execution capabilities.\n\n## Universal Solver Non-Goals\n\n- The universal solver should not skip steps for \"easy\" prompts to look fast; every prompt walks the same loop so the trace is comparable across requests.\n- Faking the evidence trail is not acceptable. Each `impulse:`, `search:local`, `search:external`, `sub_impulse:`, `candidate:`, `validation:`, `trace:`, `cache_hit:`, `source:`, `policy:`, `agent_mode:`, and `error:` link must correspond to a real recorded event.\n- Memoizing answers from a static table is not a substitute for re-running formalization, decomposition, and validation; cache hits must be recorded explicitly and link to the prior trace.\n- Hiding decomposition behind an opaque rule is not acceptable; every sub-impulse must be a first-class event the user can inspect.\n- The append-only log must not be rewritten or pruned silently. Retractions append new events that supersede earlier ones.\n- Bypassing `SolverConfig` for hard-coded behavior is not acceptable; new knobs are added to the config first, then consumed by the engine.\n- Randomized candidate generation must not become a hidden source of non-determinism; the same prompt with the same config must produce the same answer.\n\n## Append-Only Event Log Non-Goals\n\n- The event log is not a debug-only stream. It is the system of record, and the user-facing answer is a projection of it.\n- The event log is not a place for unbounded growth: events are content-addressed, deduplicated, and bounded by `max_decomposition_depth` and the source-cache TTL.\n- The event log should not leak secrets. Bearer tokens, API keys, and personal data must be redacted before they reach a link.\n- Reading the event log should not require a separate database; it must remain inspectable from CLI, HTTP, and chat surfaces.\n\n## Data Non-Goals\n\n- A large preloaded database is not the first objective.\n- Vendoring massive public datasets into the repository is not a goal.\n- Opaque binary knowledge stores are not enough unless paired with reviewable Links Notation exports.\n- Destructive memory updates should not erase history by default.\n- External web/API access should not become untracked context.\n- Duplicate names should not be forced into one meaning when evidence shows different concepts.\n\n## Product Non-Goals\n\n- The visual graph is not meant to replace chat as the primary interface.\n- The GitHub Pages demo is not expected to become a full production backend.\n- Telegram support is not meant to hide environment limits or require unsupported execution features.\n- The desktop app path is not a separate product until the library, API, and local data boundaries are stable.\n- Agent mode is not intended for unsafe use on personal or production systems without isolation.\n\n## Documentation Non-Goals\n\n- Case studies should not become marketing pages.\n- Vision documents should not imply that all long-term architecture exists today.\n- Requirements should not be marked complete until there is implementation evidence or an explicit scope boundary.\n- Research notes should not copy large external texts; they should summarize and cite sources.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

[2026-09-02T21:25:53.108Z] [STDERR] # Vision
[2026-09-02T21:25:53.108Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T21:25:53.108Z] [STDERR] Formal AI should become a symbolic assistant whose live state is an associative operational space. The assistant should not be defined by hidden neural weights or by a large memoized answer table. It should be defined by an inspectable associative network of links: user messages, source data, inferred meanings, commands, test results, generated code, failures, permissions, and final answers.
[2026-09-02T21:25:53.108Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T21:25:53.108Z] [STDERR] The associative network is the AI. The runtime should activate, extend, query, and simplify that network as work happens.
[2026-09-02T21:25:53.108Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T21:25:53.108Z] [STDERR] The fact-checked design theses behind “AI = data + algorithm,” “everything is a
[2026-09-02T21:25:53.108Z] [STDERR] link,” transformation networks, controlled self-modification, recursive
[2026-09-02T21:25:53.108Z] [STDERR] decomposition, and Markov substitution are in
[2026-09-02T21:25:53.108Z] [STDERR] [`docs/philosophy.md`](docs/philosophy.md). That guide distinguishes metaphor,
[2026-09-02T21:25:53.108Z] [STDERR] mathematical fact, implemented behavior, and target behavior.
[2026-09-02T21:25:53.108Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T21:25:53.108Z] [STDERR] This places Formal AI squarely in the tradition of [symbolic artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbolic_artificial_intelligence) (GOFAI): the link network is a [semantic network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semantic_network) in the classical sense, and intelligence is the rule-driven manipulation of human-readable symbols ([physical symbol system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_symbol_system) hypothesis, Newell & Simon 1976) rather than numeric optimization of hidden weights. The audit in [`docs/case-studies/issue-451/symbolic-ai-best-practices.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-451/symbolic-ai-best-practices.md) maps each of the field's best practices onto this associative stack.

model for this project.\n- `lino-objects-codec` remains useful for converting structured objects into reviewable Links Notation during the transition.\n\nThe dynamic type system should be expressible with doublets:\n\n```text\nType -> SubType\nSubType -> SubType\nSubType -> Value\n```\n\nThis keeps the seed model small while letting the network define new concepts, instances, relations, handlers, and rules as they are needed.\n\n## Operating Principles\n\n- Small seeds, dynamic growth: start with the smallest useful seed dataset, then construct missing knowledge on demand.\n- Transparent reasoning: every step, decision, command, data access, and answer should be traceable to links and source events.\n- Add-only history: changes requested by users or made by the assistant should be appended as events first, then projected into the current state.\n- User-queryable memory: the user should be able to ask about any relevant detail in the associative network and receive a traceable Reasoning Model\n\nThe assistant should use a universal problem-solving loop:\n\n1. Record the user message as an impulse event.\n2. Identify unknown concepts, requirements, constraints, and missing context.\n3. Search local links first, then external sources if local data is insufficient.\n4. Convert findings into link-native meanings with source metadata.\n5. Split the problem into smaller tasks until each task is executable or answerable.\n6. Draft experiments together with tests and traces.\n7. Select a passing draft, execute it where permitted, and compose its result.\n8. On failure, shrink to smaller tasks; at an unsupported leaf, extend the tool,\n   retry the leaf, then climb back up and retest the whole task.\n9. Record results, failures, and learned procedures.\n10. Return the smallest sufficient answer plus links to the relevant trace.\n\nThis loop can be implemented first as ordinary Rust logic, then increasingly represented as link substitutions, triggers, and reusable associative packages.\n\n## Universal Problem-Solving Algorithm\n\nThe reasoning loop above is the outer skeleton. The inner mechanics should be a single universal algorithm that does not assume prior knowledge of the task and works in the same shape for greetings, code generation, translation, source-checking, agent actions, or any future request:\n\n1. **Impulse**: append the raw user message as an `impulse` event in the append-only log.\n2. **Formalization**: turn the impulse into a `requirement` record. The algorithm decides — controlled by a configurable knob — whether to guess the formalization from context or to ask the user the smallest possible clarifying question.\n3. **Context and domain data**: derive the language, surface, mode flags (chat vs agent, diagnostic on/off), and the domain (greeting, code, translation, math, agent action) from the formalized requirement.\n4. **History lookup**: check whether the same or a similar requirement has been solved before; if so, reuse the prior solution and record a `cache_hit` link.\n5. **Decomposition**: when the requirement is composite (multiple clauses, \"and\", \"with tests\", \"with benchmarks\"), split it into sub-impulses and recursively formalize each one until every sub-requirement is small enough to be solved directly.\n6. **TDD-style test generation**: derive at least one executable check or assertion that any candidate solution must pass.\n7. **Draft experiments and selection**: build testable drafts by (a) reusing known parts, (b) reasoning from rules, and (c) random or evolutionary search where structure and compute budget allow; select only a test-passing draft and record why it won.\n8. **Composition**: combine selected partial solutions back into a full solution that addresses the original requirement.\n9. **Verification and recursive recovery**: run the composed solution against the whole-task test. On failure, record `trace:execution_failure`, descend to smaller tasks, and retry upward after their tests pass. At an elementary task with no method, extend the general tool and retry that leaf. Bounds on depth and retries keep this executable loop finite.\n10. **Simplification**: apply transformation rules that preserve meaning to shorten the answer and the reasoning trace. Pick the smallest sufficient form.\n11. **Documentation and presentation**: produce the user-facing reply, the Links Notation trace, and the visible evidence links. If the user asks for execution, run the code in the appropriate isolation level.\n\nEvery step writes its own event to the append-only log so the user can ask the chat why the assistant did what it did and get a traceable answer from the recorded experience.\n\n## Configurable Solver Knobs\n\nThe universal algorithm should be controlled by a small, explicit, persistable `SolverConfig` so the same engine can be tuned per surface or per user:\n\n- `guess_probability` — how often the algorithm guesses a formalization vs. asking a clarifying question (`0.0` = always ask, `1.0` = always guess).\n- `context_sensitivity` — how aggressively the algorithm uses surrounding context (previous messages, recent events) when formalizing.\n- `questioning_rigor` — how strict the clarifying questions are (`0.0` = accept almost anything, `1.0` = ask until the requirement is fully formal).\n- `max_decomposition_depth` — how deep the recursive decomposition is allowed to go.\n- `agent_mode` — whether agent mode is opted in. Off by default.\n- `diagnostic_mode` — whether diagnostic links are echoed in the user-facing reply.\n- `offline` — whether external lookups are allowed (also honored from the `FORMAL_AI_OFFLINE` environment variable).\n- `cache_ttl_seconds` — TTL for cached external sources (default ≈ two months).\n- `temperature` — controls how aggressively the formalization step collapses multiple candidate interpretations into one. Lower values bias the solver toward the highest-scoring interpretation; higher values keep more interpretations alive and trigger clarifying questions or guesses, depending on `guess_probability`. Modelled on the softmax-temperature pattern used by neural networks, but applied to discrete Wikidata-anchored interpretations and symbolic probability evidence rather than neural logits.\n\nThese knobs are deterministic: the same prompt with the same config produces the same answer. \"Random guessing\" is seeded from the impulse content hash so reproducibility is preserved.\n\n## Formalization And Temperature\n\nThe reasoning loop is built around an explicit formalization layer rather than memoized prompt → answer pairs. Every input message is first translated into Links Notation as a sequence of statements or questions and appended to memory in its original form. The translated statement is then formalized: each verb phrase is mapped to a Wikidata **P-id** (property), each noun phrase to a Wikidata **Q-id** (item), with a fallback chain to Wikipedia article links and Wiktionary entries when no Wikidata anchor exists. A candidate formalization is only accepted when the targeted concept actually mentions the surface form and matches it semantically — otherwise the candidate is recorded as `formalization_unresolved` and the next candidate is tried.\n\nMultiple plausible formalizations are scored, then a temperature-controlled selector picks among them in the same way neural networks pick among logits: lower temperature collapses onto the highest-scoring interpretation; higher temperature keeps competing interpretations alive. When two or more candidates have probabilities that are equal or close, the solver either asks the smallest clarifying question that distinguishes them or guesses according to `guess_probability` — the choice is config-driven and visible in the trace. Every interpretation, every clarifying question, every guess, every accepted formalization, and every fallback is appended to the event log so the user can ask \"why did you read it that way?\" and get a complete answer.\n\nProbability evidence must remain part of the same symbolic network. Bayesian-style evidence records and Markov-style transition records are Links Notation data with provenance, timestamps, cached-source fingerprints, and deterministic replay. They can bias candidate formalizations or answer candidates, but they never modify neural weights and never call neural inference; they only adjust symbolic posterior scores before the existing temperature and clarify-vs-guess policy runs.\n\nThe full pipeline is documented in [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md).\n\n## Growable Memory And Public Knowledge As Cache\n\nMemory should grow with use, not just with prompts. Every reasoning step, every internal decision, every external request, and every response is appended to the same log so the next similar request can reuse the prior work in part or in full. The default native store is link-cli's transactional file-mapped doublets store in the library, CLI, server, and Telegram surfaces, with doublets-web (IndexedDB / `localStorage`) on the browser; portable source and backup documents are written as `.lino` files representing Links Notation, both to disk and to additional persistent storage (browser IndexedDB, future cloud sync).\n\nTreating the internet (Wikipedia, Wikidata, Wiktionary, Wikifunctions, Rosetta Code, public APIs) as a public database and the local doublets store as a cache for that database substitutes deterministic reasoning over reviewable links for opaque GPU-backed inference. The same caching pattern carries `source:`, `fetched_at`, and `sha256` metadata per the existing `cache_ttl_seconds` policy; offline mode refuses external lookups and emits a `policy:offline` event instead of synthesizing facts.\n\n## Append-Only Event Log\n\nEvery action the algorithm takes is appended to an in-process event log before the answer is built. Each event carries a kind (`impulse`, `language_detected`, `local_search`, `external_search`, `sub_impulse`, `candidate`, `validation`, `policy`, `agent_action`, `cache_hit`, `source`, `trace`, `error`) and is identified by a content-addressed id. The event log is the system of record; the answer and the evidence links are projections of it. The user can chat over this log:\n\n- \"Why did you answer that?\" returns a meta-explanation built from the most recent trace.\n- \"What do you know about X?\" returns the links involving X.\n- \"List the facts I have contributed\" filters by user.\n- \"Forget X\" is refused unless the explicit retraction protocol is used, because the log is append-only.\n- \"Export the network\" returns the Links Notation snapshot of the seed dataset plus the visible event log.\n\n## Computation Model\n\nFormal AI should use trigger-style computation over links. A trigger can react to insertion, update, deletion, or a matched pattern in the network. Substitution rules should be first-class knowledge and should be able to express reads, writes, transformations, and simplification passes. The associative store supports five rule shapes, ranked from most reviewable to most flexible:\n\n1. **Pure data rules** — `when x do y` substitutions stored directly as doublets, executable by a simple matcher in any environment.\n2. **Compiled Rust handlers** — registered through `solver_handlers` and addressable as data so the rule index can point at them.\n3. **Compiled JS handlers** — registered through the browser worker and addressable the same way, so the same rule can have language-specific implementations; under the compiled-logic doctrine this shape is transitional — logic belongs in compiled Rust (native or WASM), and the JS registration surface remains only until the worker absorption (issue #658) completes.\n4. **Dynamically compiled Rust/JS code stored as data** — source text is itself a link payload; the runtime can compile-on-demand and cache the resulting handler.\n5. **Natural-language skills / instructions** — stored as `.lino` text, executed either by an interpreter that walks them one step at a time or by an on-demand compiler that translates them into rules in any of the four shapes above (and ultimately into native binaries when the platform allows).\n\nDeep.Foundation is a useful reference for associative packages, handlers, permissions, and code stored inside associative memory. This project adapts those ideas to local Rust, browser, and CLI modes using Link Foundation doublets instead of triplet links. `ARCHITECTURE.md` documents the data shape of each rule kind and how the trigger loop dispatches across them.\n\n## Product Shape\n\nThe same symbolic core should be available through:\n\n- Rust library API.\n- CLI chat and dataset commands.\n- OpenAI-compatible HTTP API surfaces.\n- Docker-ready microservice.\n- GitHub Pages chat demo backed by a Rust WebAssembly worker.\n- Telegram private and public chat surfaces.\n- Desktop and embedded agent modes share the same library boundary; the desktop wrapper is tracked by issue [#280](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/280).\n- VS Code extension (desktop and web/`vscode.dev`) embedding the same chat; Marketplace publication is tracked by issue [#666](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/666).\n- OpenAI-compatible backend for agentic CLIs (codex, opencode, gemini, qwen, claude, agent), and — the mirror direction — an orchestrator that drives those same CLIs as permissioned tools (issue [#703](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/703)).\n\nCode-generation tasks should be a first focus area. The assistant should generate algorithms in popular languages, compile or run generated code when the environment supports it, report execution limits honestly, and preserve logs for failed reasoning or failed execution. Browser-only mode can start with JavaScript evaluation and later experiment with WebVM.\n\n## Meaning And Identity\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

[2026-09-02T21:25:57.772Z] [STDERR] # Vision
[2026-09-02T21:25:57.772Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T21:25:57.772Z] [STDERR] Formal AI should become a symbolic assistant whose live state is an associative operational space. The assistant should not be defined by hidden neural weights or by a large memoized answer table. It should be defined by an inspectable associative network of links: user messages, source data, inferred meanings, commands, test results, generated code, failures, permissions, and final answers.
[2026-09-02T21:25:57.772Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T21:25:57.772Z] [STDERR] The associative network is the AI. The runtime should activate, extend, query, and simplify that network as work happens.
[2026-09-02T21:25:57.772Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T21:25:57.772Z] [STDERR] The fact-checked design theses behind “AI = data + algorithm,” “everything is a
[2026-09-02T21:25:57.772Z] [STDERR] link,” transformation networks, controlled self-modification, recursive
[2026-09-02T21:25:57.772Z] [STDERR] decomposition, and Markov substitution are in
[2026-09-02T21:25:57.772Z] [STDERR] [`docs/philosophy.md`](docs/philosophy.md). That guide distinguishes metaphor,
[2026-09-02T21:25:57.772Z] [STDERR] mathematical fact, implemented behavior, and target behavior.
[2026-09-02T21:25:57.772Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T21:25:57.772Z] [STDERR] This places Formal AI squarely in the tradition of [symbolic artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbolic_artificial_intelligence) (GOFAI): the link network is a [semantic network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semantic_network) in the classical sense, and intelligence is the rule-driven manipulation of human-readable symbols ([physical symbol system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_symbol_system) hypothesis, Newell & Simon 1976) rather than numeric optimization of hidden weights. The audit in [`docs/case-studies/issue-451/symbolic-ai-best-practices.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-451/symbolic-ai-best-practices.md) maps each of the field's best practices onto this associative stack.

[2026-09-02T21:26:00.690Z] [STDERR] structure should be recursive links: `defined_by` links for ontology reduction
[2026-09-02T21:26:00.690Z] [STDERR] and semantic facets for notation, annotation, denotation, and connotation. The
[2026-09-02T21:26:00.690Z] [STDERR] facet kinds themselves are meanings in the seed, so adding a new semantic view
[2026-09-02T21:26:00.690Z] [STDERR] is data growth rather than a new hardcoded language constant.
[2026-09-02T21:26:00.690Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T21:26:00.690Z] [STDERR] The semantic root should also stay compatible with Links Theory: `reference`,
[2026-09-02T21:26:00.690Z] [STDERR] `link_action`, defined connectives, quantity primitives, and self-equations are
[2026-09-02T21:26:00.690Z] [STDERR] seed meanings, and ambiguous symbols are split into distinct meanings such as
[2026-09-02T21:26:00.690Z] [STDERR] `bank_river` and `bank_money` instead of one overloaded surface.
[2026-09-02T21:26:00.690Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T21:26:00.690Z] [STDERR] Natural languages and programming languages should be translated through link-native meanings rather than through one-off text rewrites. Once a phrase has been fully formalized — verbs mapped to Wikidata P-IDs, nouns mapped to Q-IDs, fallbacks documented to Wikipedia or Wiktionary entries — translating it to another language reduces to looking up the destination-language label on the same P/Q anchor. The same mechanism translates between natural language and programming languages: formalized statements can be rendered into Rust, JavaScript, or any other target whose syntactic forms have been linked into the doublet store. Links Notation acts as the intermediate language of meaning for explanations, code generation, data imports, cross-language translation, and on-demand compilation of natural-language skills into executable code.

Decompose,\n    Compare,\n    /// Attempt the whole task first and split only what actually failed.\n    ///\n    /// The plan is discovered from evidence rather than committed to up front;\n    ///      command_overrides: BTreeMap::new(),\n            max_depth: 3,\n            pull_request: None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum DispatchError {\n    PermissionDenied,\n    MissingCli,\n    DuplicateCli(String),\n    OutputOutsideWorkspace,\n    Run(AgentRunError),\n    Replay(ReplayError),\n    Io(io::Error),\n    WorkerPanicked,\n    CompositionConflict(String),\n    Attribution(String),\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for DispatchError {\n    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            Self::PermissionDenied =>            Self::OutputOutsideWorkspace => formatter.write_str(\"output_outside_workspace\"),\n            Self::Run(error) => write!(formatter, \"run:{error}\"),\n            Self::Replay(error) =>
