Self::CompositionConflict(path) => write!(formatter, \"composition_conflict:{path}\"),\n            Self::Attribution(error) => write!(formatter, \"attribution:{error}\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for DispatchError {}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ComparisonEntry {\n    pub cli: String,\n    pub task: String,\n    pub passed: bool,\n    pub diff_size: u64,\n    pub wall_time_ms: u64,\n    pub session_file: String,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ComparisonLedger {\n    pub schema: String,\n    pub selection_rule: String,\n    pub entries: Vec<ComparisonEntry>,\n    pub winner: Option<String>,\n}\n\nimpl ComparisonLedger {\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn select_winner(entries: &[ComparisonEntry]) -> Option<String> {\n        let mut candidates = entries\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|entry| entry.passed)\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n        candidates.sort_by(|left, right| {\n            left.diff_size\n                .cmp(&right.diff_size)\n                .then_with(|| left.wall_time_ms.cmp(&right.wall_time_ms))\n                .then_with(|| left.cli.cmp(&right.cli))\n                .then_with(|| left.session_file.cmp(&right.session_file))\n        });\n        candidates.first().map(|entry| entry.cli.clone())\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct DispatchReport {\n    pub schema: String,\n    pub mode: DispatchMode,\n    pub tasks: Vec<String>,\n    pub sessions: Vec<AgentSession>,\n    pub ledger: ComparisonLedger,\n    pub composed_changes: Vec<WorkspaceChange>,\n    /// Present exactly for [`DispatchMode::Incremental`]: what was attempted,\n    /// what was split, and what stayed blocked. Absent from the other modes'\n    /// JSON entirely, so an existing report still parses.\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub incremental: Option<IncrementalTrace>,\n}\n\npub fn dispatch_agents(config: &DispatchConfig) -> Result<DispatchReport, DispatchError> {\n    if !config.permission.permits(&config.workspace) {\n        return Err(DispatchError::PermissionDenied);\n    }\n    if config.clis.is_empty() {\n        return Err(DispatchError::MissingCli);\n    }\n    let mut unique_clis = BTreeSet::new();\n    for cli in &config.clis {\n        if !unique_clis.insert(cli) {\n            return Err(DispatchError::DuplicateCli(cli.clone()));\n        }\n    }\n    let workspace = config.workspace.canonicalize().map_err(DispatchError::Io)?;\n    if let Some(pull_request) = &config.pull_request {\n        if config.mode != DispatchMode::Incremental {\n            return Err(DispatchError::Attribution(\n                \"incremental_mode_required\".to_string(),\n            ));\n        }\n        prepare_attribution(&workspace, pull_request)?;\n    }\n    let prospective_output = prospective_canonical(&config.output_dir)?;\n    if prospective_output == workspace || !prospective_output.starts_with(&workspace) {\n        return Err(DispatchError::OutputOutsideWorkspace);\n    }\n    prepare_output_dir(&config.output_dir)?;\n    let output_dir = config\n        .output_dir\n        .canonicalize()\n        .map_err(DispatchError::Io)?;\n    if config.mode == DispatchMode::Incremental {\n        // The whole task is the plan until a failure says otherwise, so this\n        // mode never builds a job list: it discovers one.\n        return dispatch_incrementally(config, &workspace, &output_dir);\n    }\n    let tasks = match config.mode {\n        DispatchMode::Compare => vec![config.task.clone(); config.clis.len()],\n        DispatchMode::Incremental => unreachable!(\"incremental dispatch returned above\"),\n        DispatchMode::Decompose => {\n            let decomposition = decompose_task(&config.task, config.max_depth);\n            let leaves = decomposition.leaves();\n            if leaves.is_empty() {\n                vec![config.task.clone()]\n            } else {\n                leaves.into_iter().map(|leaf| leaf.text.clone()).collect()\n            }\n        }\n    };\n    let jobs = match config.mode {\n        DispatchMode::Incremental => unreachable!(\"incremental dispatch returned above\"),\n        DispatchMode::Compare => config\n            .clis\n            .iter()\n            .cloned()\n            .zip(tasks.iter().cloned())\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),\n        DispatchMode::Decompose => tasks\n            .iter()\n            .cloned()\n            .enumerate()\n            .map(|(index, task)| (config.clis[index % config.clis.len()].clone(), task))\n            .collect(),\n    };\n    let mut handles = Vec::new();\n    for (index, (cli, task)) in jobs.into_iter().enumerate() {\n        let candidate_id = format!(\"{index:03}-{}\", safe_name(&cli));\n        let candidate = config.output_dir.join(\"candidates\").join(&candidate_id);\n        copy_workspace(&workspace, &candidate, &output_dir).map_err(DispatchError::Io)?;\n        let orchestration_home = output_dir.join(\"native-sessions\").join(candidate_id);\n        let run = candidate_run_config(config, &cli, task, &candidate, &orchestration_home);\n        handles.push((\n            index,\n            cli,\n            candidate,\n            thread::spawn(move || run_agent(&run)),\n        ));\n    }\n    let mut completed = Vec::new();\n    let mut worker_error = None;\n    for (index, cli, candidate, handle) in handles {\n        match handle.join() {\n            Ok(Ok(session)) => completed.push((index, cli, candidate, session)),\n            Ok(Err(error)) => {\n                worker_error.get_or_insert(DispatchError::Run(error));\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                worker_error.get_or_insert(DispatchError::WorkerPanicked);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    if let Some(error) = worker_error {\n        return Err(error);\n    }\n    completed.sort_by_key(|(index, _, _, _)| *index);\n    let mut entries = Vec::new();\n    for (index, cli, _, session) in &completed {\n        let relative = format!(\"sessions/{index:03}-{}.json\", safe_name(cli));\n        let path = config.output_dir.join(&relative);\n        write_session(&path, session).map_err(DispatchError::Replay)?;\n        entries.push(ComparisonEntry {\n            cli: cli.clone(),\n            task: session.task.clone(),\n            passed: session.passed(),\n            diff_size: session.diff_size(),\n            wall_time_ms: session.wall_time_ms,\n            session_file: relative,\n        });\n    }\n    let winner = if config.mode == DispatchMode::Compare {\n        ComparisonLedger::select_winner(&entries)\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n    let composed_changes = compose(config.mode, &workspace, &completed, winner.as_deref())?;\n    let ledger = ComparisonLedger {\n        schema: \"formal-ai-comparison-ledger-v1\".to_string(),\n        selection_rule: \"pass,diff_size,wall_time,cli,session_file\".to_string(),\n        entries,\n        winner,\n    };\n    let ledger_bytes = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&ledger)\n        .map_err(|error| DispatchError::Replay(ReplayError::Json(error)))?;\n    let mut rendered = ledger_bytes;\n    rendered.push(b'\\n');\n    fs::write(config.output_dir.join(\"comparison-ledger.json\"), rendered)\n        .map_err(DispatchError::Io)?;\n    Ok(DispatchReport {\n        schema: \"formal-ai-dispatch-report-v1\".to_string(),\n        mode: config.mode,\n        tasks,\n        sessions: completed\n            .into_iter()\n            .map(|(_, _, _, session)| session)\n            .collect(),\n        ledger,\n        composed_changes,\n        incremental: None,\n    })\n}\n\nfn prospective_canonical(path: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, DispatchError> {\n    if path\n        .components()\n        .any(|component| matches!(component, std::path::Component::ParentDir))\n    {\n        return Err(DispatchError::OutputOutsideWorkspace);\n    }\n    let absolute = if path.is_absolute() {\n        path.to_path_buf()\n    } else {\n        std::env::current_dir()\n            .map_err(DispatchError::Io)?\n            .join(path)\n    };\n    let mut ancestor = absolute.as_path();\n    let mut suffix = Vec::new();\n    while !ancestor.exists() {\n        let name = ancestor.file_name().ok_or_else(|| {\n            DispatchError::Io(io::Error::new(\n                io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,\n                \"output_path_has_no_existing_ancestor\",\n            ))\n        })?;\n        suffix.push(name.to_os_string());\n        ancestor = ancestor.parent().ok_or_else(|| {\n            DispatchError::Io(io::Error::new(\n                io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,\n                \"output_path_has_no_parent\",\n            ))\n        })?;\n    }\n    let mut resolved = ancestor.canonicalize().map_err(DispatchError::Io)?;\n    for name in suffix.into_iter().rev() {\n        resolved.push(name);\n    }\n    Ok(resolved)\n}\n\nfn prepare_output_dir(path: &Path) -> Result<(), DispatchError> {\n    if path.exists() {\n        let mut entries = fs::read_dir(path).map_err(DispatchError::Io)?;\n        if entries\n            .next()\n            .transpose()\n            .map_err(DispatchError::Io)?\n            .is_some()\n        {\n            return Err(DispatchError::Io(io::Error::new(\n                io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists,\n                \"orchestration_output_not_empty\",\n            )));\n        }\n    }\n    fs::create_dir_all(path.join(\"candidates\")).map_err(DispatchError::Io)?;\n    fs::create_dir_all(path.join(\"sessions\")).map_err(DispatchError::Io)\n}\n\npub(super) fn candidate_run_config(\n    dispatch: &DispatchConfig,\n    cli: &str,\n    task: String,\n    workspace: &Path,\n    orchestration_home: &Path,\n) -> AgentRunConfig {\n    let mut run = AgentRunConfig::new(cli, task, workspace)\n        .with_permission(AgentRunPermission::grant_for(workspace));\n    run.model.clone_from(&dispatch.model);\n    run.base_url.clone_from(&dispatch.base_url);\n    run.target = dispatch.target;\n    run.timeout = dispatch.timeout;\n    run.allowlisted_agent_commands\n        .clone_from(&dispatch.allowlisted_agent_commands);\n    run.allowlisted_commands\n        .clone_from(&dispatch.allowlisted_commands);\n    run.verification.clone_from(&dispatch.verification);\n    run.controller_program\n        .clone_from(&dispatch.controller_program);\n    run.orchestration_home = Some(orchestration_home.to_path_buf());\n    run.command_override = dispatch.command_overrides.get(cli).cloned();\n    run\n}\n\nfn compose(\n    mode: DispatchMode,\n    workspace: &Path,\n    completed: &[(usize, String, PathBuf, AgentSession)],\n    winner: Option<&str>,\n) -> Result<Vec<WorkspaceChange>, DispatchError> {\n    match mode {\n        DispatchMode::Compare => {\n            let selected = completed\n                .iter()\n                .find(|(_, cli, _, _)| Some(cli.as_str()) == winner);\n            if let Some((_, _, candidate, session)) = selected {\n                apply_changes(workspace, candidate, &session.changes).map_err(DispatchError::Io)?;\n                return Ok(session.changes.clone());\n            }\n            Ok(Vec::new())\n        }\n        DispatchMode::Decompose => compose_decomposed(workspace, completed),\n        // Incremental runs compose as they go: a passing attempt's effects are\n        // applied to the workspace before the next attempt copies it.\n        DispatchMode::Incremental => unreachable!(\"incremental dispatch composes during the run\"),\n    }\n}\n\nfn compose_decomposed(\n    workspace: &Path,\n    completed: &[(usize, String, PathBuf, AgentSession)],\n) -> Result<Vec<WorkspaceChange>, DispatchError> {\n    let mut owners = BTreeMap::<String, (PathBuf, WorkspaceChange)>::new();\n    for (_, _, candidate, session) in completed\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|(_, _, _, session)| session.passed())\n    {\n        for change in &session.changes {\n            if let Some((_, prior)) = owners.get(&change.path) {\n                if prior != change {\n                    return Err(DispatchError::CompositionConflict(change.path.clone()));\n                }\n            } else {\n                owners.insert(change.path.clone(), (candidate.clone(), change.clone()));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    for (candidate, change) in owners.values() {\n        validate_changes(workspace, candidate, std::slice::from_ref(change))\n            .map_err(DispatchError::Io)?;\n    }\n    for (candidate, change) in owners.values() {\n        apply_changes(workspace, candidate, std::slice::from_ref(change))\n            .map_err(DispatchError::Io)?;\n    }\n    Ok(owners.into_values().map(|(_, change)| change).collect())\n}\n\npub(super) fn safe_name(value: &str) -> String {\n    value\n        .chars()\n        .map(|character| {\n            if character.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(character, '-' | '_') {\n                character\n            } else {\n                '_'\n            }\n        })\n        .collect()\n}\n//! Incremental, failure-driven dispatch to external agentic CLIs.\n//!\n//! [`super::dispatch`]'s decompose mode splits the task once, up front, and\n//! sends every leaf out in parallel. That commits to a plan before any evidence\n//! exists: if a leaf turns out to be too large for the CLI, nothing splits it,\n//! and if the whole task was solvable as given, the split was wasted work.\n//!\n//! This mode inverts the order. The whole task is attempted first. Only a\n//! failure justifies a split, the pieces are executed by the same rule, and the\n//! parent is re-attempted once its pieces pass. The controller is\n//! [`crate::recursive_execution::solve_recursively`] and the splitter is\n//! [`crate::task_decomposition::SplittingExecutor`], so the shrink-on-failure\n//! protocol is the repository's own -- this module only supplies the tool\n//! boundary: an attempt is one recorded agent session in a copy of the\n//! workspace, and a passing attempt's effects are applied to the workspace\n//! before the next one starts.\n//!\n//! Extending the tool has a concrete meaning here. This controller cannot add a\n//! capability to somebody else's CLI, but it was given a list of CLIs; an\n//! irreducible task that one CLI failed is escalated to the next one that has\n//! not tried it. When the list is exhausted the task is reported blocked, with\n//! the evidence of every attempt, which is exactly the input the review-gated\n//! learning path needs.\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\n\nuse super::attribution::{commit_verified_effect, validate_effect_attribution};\nuse super::dispatch::{\n    ComparisonEntry, ComparisonLedger, DispatchConfig, DispatchError, DispatchMode, DispatchReport,\n    candidate_run_config, safe_name,\n};\nuse super::observe_orchestration_session;\nuse super::replay::write_session;\nuse super::runner::{AgentSession, run_agent, verify_workspace};\nuse super::workspace::{WorkspaceChange, apply_changes, copy_workspace};\nuse crate::client_contract_learning::learn_client_contracts;\nuse crate::links_format::push_lino_node;\nuse crate::recursive_execution::{\n    RecursiveRun, RecursiveTask, TaskAttempt, TaskExecutor, solve_recursively,\n};\nuse crate::task_decomposition::SplittingExecutor;\n\nconst COMPOSED_VERIFIER: &str = \"composed-verifier\";\n\n/// One attempted task, in execution order. The index into\n/// [`DispatchReport::sessions`] is this step's position in `steps`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct IncrementalStep {\n    /// Identity of the executed task node.\n    pub task_id: String,\n    /// The task text handed to the CLI.\n    pub task: String,\n    /// CLI that ran this attempt, or `composed-verifier` when the controller\n    /// accepted already-composed child effects without another agent call.\n    pub cli: String,\n    /// Whether the session and its verification passed.\n    pub passed: bool,\n    /// Recorded session file, relative to the output directory.\n    pub session_file: String,\n}\n\n/// One split the controller performed after a failure.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct IncrementalSplit {\n    /// The task that failed and was split.\n    pub task: String,\n    /// Evidence from the failing attempt that justified the split.\n    pub failure_evidence: String,\n    /// How many splits already happened above this task.\n    pub split_depth: u8,\n    /// Sub-tasks produced, in composition order. Empty means the splitter\n    /// declared the task irreducible.\n    pub children: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n/// A task no CLI in the list could solve, written out for review.\n///\n/// This is the run's own request to be extended: it names the task, every CLI\n/// that already tried it, and the evidence each attempt produced. Nothing here\n/// activates anything -- promotion stays behind the same review gate\n/// [`crate::task_decomposition::TaskStrategyLedger`] applies to a learned\n/// decomposition strategy.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct IncrementalProposal {\n    /// Stable identity of this proposal, from the task and its evidence.\n    pub id: String,\n    /// The irreducible task that stayed unsolved.\n    pub task: String,\n    /// Every CLI that attempted it, in the order they were tried.\n    pub tried_clis: Vec<String>,\n    /// Evidence from each failing attempt, in execution order.\n    pub failure_evidence: Vec<String>,\n    /// Always `human_review_required`: a run cannot approve its own extension.\n    pub status: String,\n}\n\nimpl IncrementalProposal {\n    /// This proposal as Links Notation, in the review-gated learning vocabulary.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn links_notation(&self) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::new();\n        push_lino_node(&mut out, 0, \"incremental_proposal\", Some(&self.id));\n        push_lino_node(&mut out, 2, \"task\", Some(&self.task));\n        for cli in &self.tried_clis {\n            push_lino_node(&mut out, 2, \"tried_cli\", Some(cli));\n        }\n        for evidence in &self.failure_evidence {\n            push_lino_node(&mut out, 2, \"failure_evidence\", Some(evidence));\n        }\n        push_lino_node(&mut out, 2, \"status\", Some(&self.status));\n        out\n    }\n}\n\n/// Everything the failure-driven run did, in the order it did it.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct IncrementalTrace {\n    /// Schema identity of this trace.\n    pub schema: String,\n    /// Whether the root task ended up passing.\n    pub solved: bool,\n    /// Deepest level of failure-driven splitting the run reached.\n    pub split_depth_reached: u8,\n    /// Every attempt, in execution order.\n    pub steps: Vec<IncrementalStep>,\n    /// Every split the controller requested.\n    pub splits: Vec<IncrementalSplit>,\n    /// Irreducible tasks that no CLI in the list could solve.\n    pub blocked_tasks: Vec<String>,\n    /// One review request per blocked task, mirrored to `proposals.lino`.\n    pub proposals: Vec<IncrementalProposal>,\n}\n\n/// Run one task incrementally and report every attempt, split, and effect.\npub(super) fn dispatch_incrementally(\n    config: &DispatchConfig,\n    workspace: &Path,\n    output_dir: &Path,\n) -> Result<DispatchReport, DispatchError> {\n    let root = RecursiveTask::leaf(root_id(&config.task), config.task.clone());\n    let mut executor = SplittingExecutor::new(AgentExecutor::new(config, workspace, output_dir));\n    let run = solve_recursively(&root, &mut executor);\n    let splits = executor\n        .splits()\n        .iter()\n        .map(|split| IncrementalSplit {\n            task: split.goal.clone(),\n            failure_evidence: split.failure_evidence.clone(),\n            split_depth: split.split_depth,\n            children: split.children.clone(),\n        })\n        .collect();\n    let agent = executor.into_inner();\n    if let Some(error) = agent.error {\n        return Err(error);\n    }\n    write_learning(output_dir, &agent.steps, &agent.sessions)?;\n\n    let entries = agent\n        .steps\n        .iter()\n        .zip(agent.sessions.iter())\n        .map(|(step, session)| ComparisonEntry {\n            cli: step.cli.clone(),\n            task: session.task.clone(),\n            passed: session.passed(),\n            diff_size: session.diff_size(),\n            wall_time_ms: session.wall_time_ms,\n            session_file: step.session_file.clone(),\n        })\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n    let proposals = proposals(&run, &agent.steps);\n    write_proposals(&config.output_dir, &proposals)?;\n    let trace = IncrementalTrace {\n        schema: \"formal-ai-incremental-trace-v1\".to_string(),\n        solved: run.is_passed(),\n        split_depth_reached: run.split_depth_reached(),\n        steps: agent.steps,\n        splits,\n        blocked_tasks: blocked_tasks(&run),\n        proposals,\n    };\n    Ok(DispatchReport {\n        schema: \"formal-ai-dispatch-report-v1\".to_string(),\n        mode: DispatchMode::Incremental,\n        tasks: trace.steps.iter().map(|step| step.task.clone()).collect(),\n        sessions: agent.sessions,\n        ledger: ComparisonLedger {\n            schema: \"formal-ai-comparison-ledger-v1\".to_string(),\n            selection_rule: \"pass,diff_size,wall_time,cli,session_file\".to_string(),\n            entries,\n            winner: None,\n        },\n        composed_changes: agent.changes,\n        incremental: Some(trace),\n    })\n}\n\n/// Feed the exact execution sessions into the existing proposal-only client\n/// contract learner. Incremental execution and auto-learning are one lifecycle:\n/// a run always preserves what it learned, while promotion remains a separate\n/// human decision enforced by the learner itself.\nfn write_learning(\n    output_dir: &Path,\n    steps: &[IncrementalStep],\n    sessions: &[AgentSession],\n) -> Result<(), DispatchError> {\n    let observations = steps\n        .iter()\n        .zip(sessions)\n        .filter(|(step, _)| step.cli != COMPOSED_VERIFIER)\n        .map(|(step, session)| observe_orchestration_session(session, &step.session_file))\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n    let learning = learn_client_contracts(&observations, &crate::seed::client_integrations());\n    std::fs::write(output_dir.join(\"learning.lino\"), learning.links_notation())\n        .map_err(DispatchError::Io)\n}\n\n/// Goals of the irreducible tasks a run could not solve, in execution order.\nfn blocked_tasks(run: &RecursiveRun) -> Vec<String> {\n    run.blocked_leaves()\n        .into_iter()\n        .map(|leaf| leaf.task.goal.clone())\n        .collect()\n}\n\nfn root_id(task: &str) -> String {\n    crate::engine::stable_id(\"dispatch_task\", task)\n}\n\n/// One review request per blocked task, in execution order.\n///\n/// A run that ends with something unsolved has produced the one thing the\n/// learning path cannot invent: a named task, the tools that were tried, and\n/// what each of them reported. Writing it out is what makes the next extension\n/// reviewable rather than guessed.\nfn proposals(run: &RecursiveRun, steps: &[IncrementalStep]) -> Vec<IncrementalProposal> {\n    run.blocked_leaves()\n        .into_iter()\n        .map(|leaf| {\n            let attempts = steps.iter().filter(|step| step.task_id == leaf.task.id);\n            let mut tried_clis: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n            for attempt in attempts {\n                if !tried_clis.contains(&attempt.cli) {\n                    tried_clis.push(attempt.cli.clone());\n                }\n            }\n            let failure_evidence: Vec<String> = leaf\n                .attempts\n                .iter()\n                .filter(|attempt| !attempt.passed)\n                .map(|attempt| attempt.evidence.clone())\n                .collect();\n            let id = crate::engine::stable_id(\n                \"incremental_proposal\",\n                &format!(\"{}|{}\", leaf.task.id, failure_evidence.join(\"|\")),\n            );\n            IncrementalProposal {\n                id,\n                task: leaf.task.goal.clone(),\n                tried_clis,\n                failure_evidence,\n                status: \"human_review_required\".to_string(),\n            }\n        })\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// Mirror the proposals next to the report, in the notation review reads.\n///\n/// A run with nothing blocked writes the file anyway, empty but for its header:\n/// \"no proposal\" and \"the run never got that far\" are different answers, and a\n/// missing file cannot tell them apart.\nfn write_proposals(\n    output_dir: &Path,\n    proposals: &[IncrementalProposal],\n) -> Result<(), DispatchError> {\n    let mut document = String::new();\n    push_lino_node(&mut document, 0, \"incremental_proposals\", None);\n    for proposal in proposals {\n        document.push_str(&proposal.links_notation());\n    }\n    std::fs::write(output_dir.join(\"proposals.lino\"), document).map_err(DispatchError::Io)\n}\n\n/// What an attempt observed, as the splitter and the reviewer read it.\n///\n/// Machine evidence, not prose: each field is one whitespace-free `key:value`\n/// token, so the record stays greppable and the split decision is made from\n/// facts a reader can check against the recorded session.\nfn evidence_of(cli: &str, session: &AgentSession) -> String {\n    let verification = session\n        .verification\n        .iter()\n        .map(|result| format!(\"{}={}\", result.program, result.passed))\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n        .join(\",\");\n    let exit = session\n        .exit_code\n        .map_or_else(|| \"none\".to_string(), |code| code.to_string());\n    [\n        format!(\"cli:{cli}\"),\n        format!(\"status:{:?}\", session.status),\n        format!(\"exit:{exit}\"),\n        format!(\"verification:{verification}\"),\n    ]\n    .join(\" \")\n}\n\n/// The tool boundary: one attempt is one recorded agent session.\nstruct AgentExecutor<'config> {\n    config: &'config DispatchConfig,\n    workspace: PathBuf,\n    output_dir: PathBuf,\n    sessions: Vec<AgentSession>,\n    steps: Vec<IncrementalStep>,\n    changes: Vec<WorkspaceChange>,\n    /// How many CLIs each task has already consumed, keyed by task identity.\n    escalations: BTreeMap<String, usize>,\n    /// The first controller error, kept because the executor trait has no way\n    /// to report one. A run that hit it is reported as an error, never as a\n    /// failed task: a controller fault is not evidence about the task.\n    error: Option<DispatchError>,\n}\n\nimpl<'config> AgentExecutor<'config> {\n    fn new(config: &'config DispatchConfig, workspace: &Path, output_dir: &Path) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            config,\n            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n            output_dir: output_dir.to_path_buf(),\n            sessions: Vec::new(),\n            steps: Vec::new(),\n            changes: Vec::new(),\n            escalations: BTreeMap::new(),\n            error: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Which CLI runs this task next: the first one, then one further along the\n    /// list for each escalation this self.config.clis[index.min(self.config.clis.len() - 1)].clone()\n    }\n\n    fn record(&mut self, error: DispatchError) {\n        if self.error.is_none() {\n            self.error = Some(error);\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn preserve_session(\n        &mut self,\n        task: &RecursiveTask,\n        cli: String,\n        session: AgentSession,\n    ) -> TaskAttempt {\n        let index = self.sessions.len();\n        let session_file = format!(\"sessions/{index:03}-{}.json\", safe_name(&cli));\n        if let Err(error) = write_session(&self.output_dir.join(&session_file), &session) {\n            self.record(DispatchError::Replay(error));\n            return TaskAttempt::failed(\"controller_aborted\");\n        }\n        self.record_preserved_session(task, cli, session, session_file)\n    }\n\n    fn record_preserved_session(\n        &mut self,\n        task: &RecursiveTask,\n        cli: String,\n        session: AgentSession,\n        session_file: String,\n    ) -> TaskAttempt {\n        let passed = session.passed();\n        let evidence = evidence_of(&cli, &session);\n        self.steps.push(IncrementalStep {\n            task_id: task.id.clone(),\n            task: task.goal.clone(),\n            cli,\n            passed,\n            session_file,\n        });\n        self.sessions.push(session);\n        if passed {\n            TaskAttempt::passed(evidence)\n        } else {\n            TaskAttempt::failed(evidence)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl TaskExecutor for AgentExecutor<'_> {\n    fn attempt(&mut self, task: &RecursiveTask) -> TaskAttempt {\n        if self.error.is_some() {\n            return TaskAttempt::failed(\"controller_aborted\");\n        }\n        let index = self.sessions.len();\n        let cli = self.cli_for(task);\n        let candidate = self\n            .output_dir\n            .join(\"candidates\")\n            .join(format!(\"{index:03}-{}\", safe_name(&cli)));\n        if let Err(error) = copy_workspace(&self.workspace, &candidate, &self.output_dir) {\n            self.record(DispatchError::Io(error));\n            return TaskAttempt::failed(\"controller_aborted\");\n        }\n        let orchestration_home = self\n            .output_dir\n            .join(\"native-sessions\")\n            .join(format!(\"{index:03}-{}\", safe_name(&cli)));\n        let run = candidate_run_config(\n            self.config,\n            &cli,\n            task.goal.clone(),\n            &candidate,\n            &orchestration_home,\n        );\n        let session = match run_agent(&run) {\n            Ok(session) => session,\n            Err(error) => {\n                self.record(DispatchError::Run(error));\n                return TaskAttempt::failed(\"controller_aborted\");\n            }\n        };\n        let passed = session.passed();\n        let session_file = format!(\"sessions/{index:03}-{}.json\", safe_name(&cli));\n        let session_path = self.output_dir.join(&session_file);\n        if let Err(error) = write_session(&session_path, &session) {\n            self.record(DispatchError::Replay(error));\n            return TaskAttempt::failed(\"controller_aborted\");\n        }\n        if passed\n            && self.config.pull_request.is_some()\n            && let Err(error) =\n                validate_effect_attribution(&self.workspace, &session_path, &session)\n        {\n            self.record(error);\n            return TaskAttempt::failed(\"controller_aborted\");\n        }\n        // A passing attempt's effects become the starting point of the next\n        // one, so a later sub-task -- and the parent's own retry -- sees the\n        // work its predecessors did instead of a workspace that forgot it.\n        if passed {\n            if let Err(error) = apply_changes(&self.workspace, &candidate, &session.changes) {\n                self.record(DispatchError::Io(error));\n                return TaskAttempt::failed(\"controller_aborted\");\n            }\n            if let Some(pull_request) = &self.config.pull_request\n                && let Err(error) =\n                    commit_verified_effect(&self.workspace, &session_path, &session, pull_request)\n            {\n                self.record(error);\n                return TaskAttempt::failed(\"controller_aborted\");\n            }\n            for change in &session.changes {\n                self.changes.retain(|prior| prior.path != change.path);\n                self.changes.push(change.clone());\n            }\n        }\n        self.record_preserved_session(task, cli, session, session_file)\n    }\n\n    fn extend_for(&mut self, task: &RecursiveTask, _failure: &TaskAttempt) -> bool {\n        if self.error.is_some() {\n            return false;\n        }\n        let used = self.escalations.get(&task.id).copied().unwrap_or(0);\n        let next = used + 1;\n        if next >= self.config.clis.len() {\n            return false;\n        }\n        self.escalations.insert(task.id.clone(), next);\n        true\n    }\n\n    fn retry_after_children(&mut self, task: &RecursiveTask) -> TaskAttempt {\n        if self.error.is_some() {\n            return TaskAttempt::failed(\"controller_aborted\");\n        }\n        if self.config.verification.is_empty() {\n            return self.attempt(task);\n        }\n        let cli = self.cli_for(task);\n        let orchestration_home = self.output_dir.join(\"native-sessions\").join(format!(\n            \"{:03}-{}\",\n            self.sessions.len(),\n            safe_name(&cli)\n        ));\n        let run = candidate_run_config(\n            self.config,\n            &cli,\n            task.goal.clone(),\n            &self.workspace,\n            &orchestration_home,\n        );\n        match verify_workspace(&run) {\n            Ok(session) if session.passed() => {\n                self.preserve_session(task, COMPOSED_VERIFIER.to_string(), session)\n            }\n            Ok(_) => self.attempt(task),\n            Err(error) => {\n                self.record(DispatchError::Run(error));\n                TaskAttempt::failed(\"controller_aborted\")\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n//! Grounded, verified workspace transformations learned from coding-task runs.\n//!\n//! The planner never edits request prose. It compiles a bounded transformation,\n//! reads the client-owned bytes, executes the transformation in memory, applies\n//! a compact edit or bounded replace-all operation, and accepts success only\n//! after an exact content-digest observation.         &updated,\n                );\n            }\n\n    if result_for_path(\n        current_turn,\n        Capability::Write,\n        &rewrite.target,\n        Some(&updated),\n    )\n grounded_rewrite(task: &str) -> Option<GroundedRewrite> {\n    let (target, old_clause, new_clause) = compose_edit_request(task)?;\n    let quoted = quoted_segments(task);\n    let operands = match quoted.as_slice() {\n        [old, new] => Some((old.clone(), new.clone())),\n        _ if seed::lexicon().mentions_role(\n            seed::ROLE_CODING_IDENTIFIER_RENAME_ACTION,\n            &task.to_lowercase(),\n        ) =>\n        {\n            Some((\n                identifier_tokens(&old_clause).next_back()?.to_owned(),\n &str) -> Option<(String, String)> {\n    const MAX_SUFFIX_BYTES: usize = 4096;\n    let mut starts = source\n        .match_indices('\\n')\n        .map(|(index, _)| index + 1)\n        .filter(|start| *start < source.len())\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n    starts.insert(0, 0);\n    for start in starts.into_iter().rev() {\n        let suffix = &source[start..];\n        if .is_some_and(|first| first.is_ascii_alphabetic() || first == '_')\n        && characters.all(|character| character.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || character == '_')\n        && !seed::lexicon()\n retry_after_children(&mut self, task: &RecursiveTask) -> TaskAttempt {\n        if self.error.is_some() {\n            return TaskAttempt::failed(\"controller_aborted\");\n        }\n        if self.config.verification.is_empty() {\n            return self.attempt(task);\n        }\n        let cli = self.cli_for(task);\n        let orchestration_home = self.output_dir.join(\"native-sessions\").join(format!(\n            \"{:03}-{}\",\n            self.sessions.len(),\n            safe_name(&cli)\n        ));\n        let run = candidate_run_config(\n            self.config,\n            &cli,\n            task.goal.clone(),\n            &self.workspace,\n            &orchestration_home,\n        );\n        match verify_workspace(&run) {\n            Ok(session) if session.passed() => {\n                self.preserve_session(task, COMPOSED_VERIFIER.to_string(), session)\n            }\n            Ok(_) => self.attempt(task),\n            Err(error) => {\n                self.record(DispatchError::Run(error));\n                TaskAttempt::failed(\"controller_aborted\")\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n//! Execution state machine for a composed general change plan.\n\nuse serde_json::json;\n\nuse super::general_planner::{\n    compose_general_change_plan, GeneralChangePlan, GeneralPlanMode, PLAN_PATH,\n};\nuse super::planner::{\n    fetch_arguments, plan_one, tool_for, write_arguments, AgenticPlan, Capability,\n};\nuse super::progress::Progress;\nuse super::tool_result;\nuse crate::protocol::ChatMessage;\n\nconst EXPECTED_PLACEHOLDER: &str = concat!(\"{\", \"expected\", \"}\");\nconst OBSERVED_PLACEHOLDER: &str = concat!(\"{\", \"observed\", \"}\");\nconst PLAN_PLACEHOLDER: &str = concat!(\"{\", \"plan\", \"}\");\nconst PLAN_PATH_PLACEHOLDER: &str = concat!(\"{\", \"plan_path\", \"}\");\n\npub(super) fn plan_general_change_step(\n    messages: &[ChatMessage],\n    tool_names: &[&str],\n    plan: &GeneralChangePlan,\n) -> AgenticPlan {\n    let progress = Progress::scan(messages);\n    // Reading the work item is an attempt to find out whether anything *can* be\n    // executed, not a step the request named. A read that comes back missing or\n    // empty therefore answers that question — the capability is unavailable —\n    // and the run continues to record the reference. Reporting the fetch as the\n    // run's failure would replace the honest terminal state of issue #904 with\n    // a transport message about a URL the user never asked to see.\n    let work_item_unreadable = plan.mode == GeneralPlanMode::RepositoryWorkItem\n        && progress\n            .latest_failure()\n            .is_some_and(|failure| failure.capability == Capability::Fetch);\n    if let Some(failure) = progress.latest_failure().filter(|_| !work_item_unreadable) {\n        if failure.capability == Capability::Write {\n            let path = failure.arguments.as_deref().and_then(tool_argument_path);\n            if let (Some(path), Some(read_tool)) =\n                (path.as_deref(), tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Read))\n                && progress.failed_write_count_for(path) == 1 {\n                    return plan_one(read_tool, read_arguments(path));\n                }\n            // The plan event is auxiliary. A write-only client cannot perform\n            // the preferred read-before-retry recovery, but its failure must\n            // not swallow the user's primary literal-file write.\n            if path.as_deref() == Some(PLAN_PATH)\n                && plan.mode == GeneralPlanMode::LiteralFile\n                && tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Read).is_none()\n                && progress.failed_write_count_for(PLAN_PATH) == 1\n                && let Some(write_tool) = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Write) {\n                    return plan_one(write_tool, write_arguments(&plan.target, &plan.content));\n                }\n            // Recovery is exhausted, but the failed call is not the last word:\n            // run the check the plan itself named so the report can carry the\n            // status the workspace answered with rather than a transport\n            // message alone (issue #916, rung R916-01).\n            if plan.mode != GeneralPlanMode::RepositoryWorkItem\n                && !plan.verification_command.trim().is_empty()\n                && progress.count(Capability::Run) == 0\n                && let Some(run_tool) = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Run) {\n                    return plan_one(\n                        run_tool,\n                        json!({ \"command\": plan.verification_command }).to_string(),\n                    );\n                }\n            return AgenticPlan::Final(tool_result::render_failure(\n                path.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"write\"),\n                &failure.detail,\n                &plan.goal,\n            ));\n        }\n        // A failed run is reported as the command that failed and the status it\n        // exited with, not as an anonymous \"run\" step (issues #905 and #908).\n        if failure.capability == Capability::Run\n            && let Some(report) = tool_result::failed_verification(\n                &progress.run_outputs,\n                &plan.verification_command,\n                &plan.goal,\n            ) {\n                return AgenticPlan::Final(report);\n            }\n        // A client may require an attempted read before creating a missing\n        // file. Whether that read found bytes or reported absence, retry the\n        // original write once; its per-target failure budget remains bounded.\n        let recovering_missing_write = failure.capability == Capability::Read\n            && progress.previous_attempt().is_some_and(|previous| {\n                previous.capability == Capability::Write && !previous.succeeded\n            });\n        if !recovering_missing_write {\n            return AgenticPlan::Final(tool_result::render_failure(\n                capability_label(failure.capability),\n                &failure.detail,\n                &plan.goal,\n            ));\n        }\n    }\n    let recovering_write = progress.last() == Some(Capability::Read)\n        && progress.previous_attempt().is_some_and(|previous| {\n            previous.capability == Capability::Write && !previous.succeeded\n        });\n    if recovering_write\n        && let (Some(tool), Some(arguments)) = (\n            tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Write),\n            progress\n                .previous_attempt()\n                .and_then(|attempt| attempt.arguments.as_deref()),\n        ) {\n            return plan_one(tool, arguments.to_owned());\n        }\n    // A repository work item names an issue, not an artifact. Recording the\n    // reference and stopping is what issue #904 reported: nothing the request\n    // asked for was ever produced. The issue itself is where the artifact is\n    // named, so read it before concluding that nothing can be executed — the\n    // capability is only genuinely unavailable once the fetch has been tried.\n    if plan.mode == GeneralPlanMode::RepositoryWorkItem {\n        if let Some(fetched) = repository_work_item_objective(plan, &progress) {\n            if let Some(step) = plan_work_item_execution(&fetched, messages, tool_names) {\n                return step;\n            }\n        } else if let Some(tool) = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Fetch)\n            && !progress\n                .attempted_fetches\n                .iter()\n                .any(|url| url == &plan.target)\n            {\n                return plan_one(tool, fetch_arguments(&plan.target));\n            }\n    }\n    if let Some(tool) = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Write) {\n        let plan_attempted = progress.attempted_write_for(PLAN_PATH);\n        let plan_written = progress.successful_write_for(PLAN_PATH);\n        if !plan_attempted {\n            return plan_one(tool, write_arguments(PLAN_PATH, &plan.links_notation()));\n        }\n        if plan.mode == GeneralPlanMode::LiteralFile\n            && !progress.successful_write_for(&plan.target)\n            && (plan_written || plan_attempted)\n        {\n            return plan_one(tool, write_arguments(&plan.target, &plan.content));\n        }\n    }\n    if let Some(tool) = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Run) {\n        let runs = progress.successful_count(Capability::Run);\n        match plan.mode {\n            GeneralPlanMode::CommandOutput => {\n                if let Some(generation) = plan.steps.get(1).and_then(|step| step.command.as_deref())\n                {\n                    if runs == 0 {\n                        return plan_one(tool, json!({ \"command\": generation }).to_string());\n                    }\n                    if runs == 1 {\n                        return plan_one(\n                            tool,\n                            json!({ \"command\": plan.verification_command }).to_string(),\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            GeneralPlanMode::LiteralFile if runs == 0 => {\n                return plan_one(\n                    tool,\n                    json!({ \"command\": plan.verification_command }).to_string(),\n                );\n            }\n            // A repository work item names no verification command: the only\n            // file this run writes is the plan record, and reading it back\n            // would verify nothing but the write itself (issue #904).\n            GeneralPlanMode::LiteralFile | GeneralPlanMode::RepositoryWorkItem => {}\n        }\n    }\n    finish_general_change(plan, &progress)\n}\n\n/// Plan the next step from what the fetched work item actually asks for.\n///\n/// The real corpus decides the shape here. The issues Hive Mind dispatches say\n/// *\"implement a Hello World program in Scala\"* — a described artifact in a\n/// named language, not literal bytes — so the same coding catalog that answers\n/// that request when a user types it directly answers it here, through the\n/// execution recipe its [`SymbolicAnswer`](crate::solver::SymbolicAnswer)\n/// carries. The literal-file composer follows, for a work item that does spell\n/// out a path and its contents.\n///\n/// Returning [`None`] means the work item named nothing this sandbox can\n/// produce — an unsupported language, or prose with no artifact in it at all —\n/// which keeps `planned_not_executed` truthful rather than inventing an\n/// artifact the issue never asked for.\nfn plan_work_item_execution(\n    objective: &str,\n    messages: &[ChatMessage],\n    tool_names: &[&str],\n) -> Option<AgenticPlan> {\n    // The default configuration is the right one: the recipe wanted here is the\n    // same `write_program` answer a user typing this request directly would get,\n    // and the client — not this solver — owns execution. Opting into agent mode\n    // would only add the policy branches that answer *about* agent actions.\n    let answer = crate::solver::UniversalSolver::default().solve(objective);\n    if let Some(step) =\n        super::command_reroute::plan_symbolic_command_reroute(messages, tool_names, &answer)\n    {\n        return Some(step);\n    }\n    let executable = compose_general_change_plan(objective)\n        .filter(|executable| executable.mode != GeneralPlanMode::RepositoryWorkItem)?;\n    Some(plan_general_change_step(messages, tool_names, &executable))\n}\n\n/// The text of the issue this work item names, once the client has fetched it.\n///\n/// Only the page fetched from the plan's own target counts. A repository work\n/// item carries one URL, and answering it with whatever page happened to be\n/// fetched for some other reason this turn would plan against the wrong issue.\nfn repository_work_item_objective(plan: &GeneralChangePlan, progress: &Progress) -> Option<String> {\n    progress\n        .fetched_pages\n        .iter()\n        .find(|(url, _)| url == &plan.target)\n        .map(|(_, text)| text.clone())\n        .filter(|text| !text.trim().is_empty())\n}\n\nfn finish_general_change(plan: &GeneralChangePlan, progress: &Progress) -> AgenticPlan {\n    if plan.mode == GeneralPlanMode::RepositoryWorkItem {\n        return AgenticPlan::Final(plan.planned_not_executed_answer());\n    }\n    // The workspace gets the last word over a completion claim: a verification\n    // command that exited non-zero replaces the claim with its own report.\n    if let Some(report) = tool_result::failed_verification(\n        &progress.run_outputs,\n        &plan.verification_command,\n        &plan.goal,\n    ) {\n        return AgenticPlan::Final(report);\n    }\n    if progress.successful_count(Capability::Run) == 0 {\n        return AgenticPlan::Final(general_plan_unverified(plan));\n    }\n    if plan.mode == GeneralPlanMode::LiteralFile {\n        let observed = progress\n            .latest_successful_output(Capability::Run)\n            .and_then(tool_result::observed_payload);\n        if observed.as_deref().map(str::trim) != Some(plan.content.trim()) {\n            return AgenticPlan::Final(general_plan_mismatch(\n                plan,\n                observed.as_deref().unwrap_or_default(),\n            ));\n        }\n    }\n    AgenticPlan::Final(general_plan_completed(plan))\n}\n\n/// The completion claim is the sentence the issue quotes as the false report,\n/// so it is seeded like every other outcome of this state machine rather than\n/// typed into Rust: the words live in `data/seed/`, and the reply follows the\n/// language the request was written in.\nfn general_plan_completed(plan: &GeneralChangePlan) -> String {\n    let language = crate::language::detect(&plan.goal).slug();\n    let mut answer =\n        crate::seed::localized_response(\"general_plan_completed\", language).unwrap_or_default();\n    answer = answer.replace(\"{target}\", &plan.target);\n    answer = answer.replace(\"{command}\", &plan.verification_command);\n    answer = answer.replace(PLAN_PATH_PLACEHOLDER, PLAN_PATH);\n    answer.replace(\n        PLAN_PLACEHOLDER,\n        &crate::issue_report::fenced_block(\n            crate::issue_report::LINO_FENCE_LANGUAGE,\n            &plan.links_notation(),\n        ),\n    )\n}\n\nfn tool_argument_path(arguments: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    let value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(arguments).ok()?;\n    [\"path\", \"filePath\", \"file_path\"]\n        .iter()\n        .find_map(|key| value.get(*key).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str))\n        .map(str::to_owned)\n}\n\nfn read_arguments(path: &str) -> String {\n    json!({\n        \"path\": path,\n        \"filePath\": path,\n        \"file_path\": path,\n    })\n    .to_string()\n}\n\nconst fn capability_label(capability: Capability) -> &'static str {\n    match capability {\n        Capability::Search => \"search\",\n        Capability::Fetch => \"fetch\",\n        Capability::Read => \"read\",\n        Capability::Write => \"write\",\n        Capability::Edit => \"edit\",\n        Capability::Run => \"run\",\n        Capability::Grep => \"grep\",\n        Capability::Glob => \"glob\",\n        Capability::ListDir => \"list directory\",\n        Capability::Todo => \"todo\",\n        Capability::Subagent => \"subagent\",\n        Capability::ReadMany => \"read many\",\n        Capability::MultiEdit => \"multi-edit\",\n        Capability::AskUser => \"ask user\",\n    }\n}\n\nfn general_plan_mismatch(plan: &GeneralChangePlan, observed: &str) -> String {\n    let language = crate::language::detect(&plan.goal).slug();\n    let mut answer =\n        crate::seed::localized_response(\"general_plan_verification_mismatch\", language)\n            .unwrap_or_default();\n    answer = answer.replace(\"{target}\", &plan.target);\n    let expected = if plan.mode == GeneralPlanMode::RepositoryWorkItem {\n        plan.links_notation()\n    } else {\n        plan.content.clone()\n    };\n    answer = answer.replace(EXPECTED_PLACEHOLDER, expected.trim());\n    answer.replace(OBSERVED_PLACEHOLDER, observed.trim())\n}\n\nfn general_plan_unverified(plan: &GeneralChangePlan) -> String {\n    let language = crate::language::detect(&plan.goal).slug();\n    let mut answer =\n        crate::seed::localized_response(\"general_plan_unverified\", language).unwrap_or_default();\n    answer = answer.replace(\"{target}\", &plan.target);\n    answer.replace(\"{command}\", &plan.verification_command)\n}\n//! Deterministic fallback planner for repository change requests (issue #654).\n//!\n//! Unlike the stored recipe fixtures, this planner derives its target and payload\n//! from the formalized request.  The resulting plan is data: it is serialized to\n//! Links Notation and written before execution, so the tool transcript is an\n//! append-only record of the decision that caused the change.\nuse super::planner::{Capability, trace_route};\nuse super::shell_command_policy::prose_sentences;\nuse super::write_request::{\n    bare_surfaces, clean_cue_token, clean_content, clean_path_token, cued_write_target,\n    first_action_cue_end, first_content_lead_end, first_prefix_lead_end,\n    honouring_pinned_first_line, looks_like_file_path, safe_relative_path, tokens,\n};\nuse crate::engine::stable_id;\nuse crate::intent_formalization::formalize_intent;\nuse crate::seed::{self, Slot};\nuse crate::self_ast_census::{self, CensusResolution};\nuse std::fmt::Write as _;\n/// Workspace-relative event-log artifact written before a general plan executes.\npub const PLAN_PATH: &str = \".formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino\";\nconst TARGET_PLACEHOLDER: &str = \"{target}\";\n/// What the bounded general planner can truthfully execute.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum GeneralPlanMode {\n    /// Write literal request content to a workspace-relative file.\n    LiteralFile,\n    /// Capture the output of an explicitly quoted command in a file.\n    CommandOutput,\n    /// Persist a referenced repository work item without fabricating a patch.\n    RepositoryWorkItem,\n}\nimpl GeneralPlanMode {\n    const fn slug(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            Self::LiteralFile => \"literal_file\",\n            Self::CommandOutput => \"command_output\",\n            Self::RepositoryWorkItem => \"repository_work_item\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n/// Where a composed plan can honestly end (issue #904).\n///\n/// A plan whose steps all operate on the plan record itself changes nothing the\n/// request named, and reading that record back verifies only that the run wrote\n/// it. Such a plan reaches [`PlanTerminalState::PlannedNotExecuted`], never a\n/// success state.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum PlanTerminalState {\n    /// Every step operates on an artifact the request named.\n    Executed,\n    /// The plan was recorded; no artifact the request named was touched.\n    PlannedNotExecuted,\n}\nimpl PlanTerminalState {\n    const fn slug(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            Self::Executed => \"executed\",\n            Self::PlannedNotExecuted => \"planned_not_executed\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n/// One ordered, capability-tagged operation in a general change plan.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct GeneralPlanStep {\n    pub capability: Capability,\n    pub action: String,\n    pub expected_evidence: String,\n    pub command: Option<String>,\n}\n/// A deterministic plan composed from a formalized, previously unrecognised request.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct GeneralChangePlan {\n    pub id: String,\n    pub mode: GeneralPlanMode,\n    pub goal: String,\n    pub target: String,\n    pub content: String,\n    pub steps: Vec<GeneralPlanStep>,\n    /// The command that observes the requested artifact after the change.\n    /// Empty when the plan can name no such command, which is the only honest\n    /// answer for a plan that reaches [`PlanTerminalState::PlannedNotExecuted`].\n    pub verification_command: String,\n    pub terminal_state: PlanTerminalState,\n}\nimpl GeneralChangePlan {\n    /// Render the plan shape consumed by the driver and documented by the meta fixture.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn links_notation(&self) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::from(\"general_change_plan\\n\");\n        field(&mut out, \"id\", &self.id);\n        field(&mut out, \"execution_mode\", self.mode.slug());\n        field(&mut out, \"terminal_state\", self.terminal_state.slug());\n        field(&mut out, \"goal\", &self.goal);\n        field(&mut out, \"target\", &self.target);\n        for (index, step) in self.steps.iter().enumerate() {\n            let _ = writeln!(out, \"  step {}\", index + 1);\n            field_nested(&mut out, \"capability\", capability_slug(step.capability));\n            field_nested(&mut out, \"action\", &step.action);\n            field_nested(&mut out, \"expected_evidence\", &step.expected_evidence);\n            if let Some(command) = &step.command {\n                field_nested(&mut out, \"command\", command);\n            }\n        }\n        if !self.verification_command.is_empty() {\n            field(&mut out, \"verification_command\", &self.verification_command);\n        }\n        out\n    }\n    /// Render the terminal answer of a plan that touched nothing the request\n    /// named: planned, not executed (issue #904).\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn planned_not_executed_answer(&self) -> String {\n        const BODY_PLACEHOLDER: &str = concat!(\"{\", \"plan\", \"}\");\n        let language = crate::language::detect(&self.goal).slug();\n        seed::localized_response(\"general_plan_repository_planned\", language)\n            .unwrap_or_default()\n            .replace(TARGET_PLACEHOLDER, &self.target)\n            .replace(\"{plan_path}\", PLAN_PATH)\n            .replace(\n                BODY_PLACEHOLDER,\n                &crate::issue_report::fenced_block(\n                    crate::issue_report::LINO_FENCE_LANGUAGE,\n                    &self.links_notation(),\n                ),\n            )\n    }\n}\n/// Return the request after its first line-anchored multilingual objective marker.\n///\n/// This removes an agent-harness preamble. Requests without a marker are unchanged.\n#[must_use]\npub fn objective_text(request: &str) -> &str {\n    let lowered = request.to_lowercase();\n    first_prefix_lead_end(&lowered, seed::ROLE_REQUEST_OBJECTIVE_LEAD)\n        .filter(|(start, _)| line_anchored(&lowered, *start))\n        .and_then(|(_, end)| request.get(end..))\n        .map_or(request, str::trim)\n}\n/// Whether a marker at `start` opens its own line, so a delimiter quoted inside\n/// running prose (\"write the words request: hello to notes.txt\") does not\n/// silently truncate the request.\nfn line_anchored(text: &str, start: usize) -> bool {\n    text[..start]\n        .chars()\n        .rev()\n        .take_while(|character| *character != '\\n')\n        .all(char::is_whitespace)\n}\n#[must_use]\npub fn compose_general_change_plan(full_request: &str) -> Option<GeneralChangePlan> {\n    let request = objective_text(full_request);\n    let command_output = parse_command_output_request(request);\n    let file_request = command_output.as_ref().map_or_else(\n        || parse_write_request(request),\n        |(target, _)| Some((target.clone(), String::new())),\n    );\n    let Some((target, content)) = file_request else {\n        return compose_repository_work_plan(request);\n    };\n    // Issue #906: \"…containing Hello World, in JavaScript.\" names the bytes and,\n    // separately, the language to write them with. Only the bytes are content.\n    let content = crate::implementation_language::without_trailing_known_modifier(&content)\n        .unwrap_or(content);\n    // Issue #1066: the same request can state the bytes and, separately,\n    // constrain the line the file has to open with. The repair belongs here\n    // rather than at the call sites, because every step of the plan quotes the\n    // content it was composed from -- the verification step's expected evidence\n    // most of all -- and a plan whose steps disagree with its own bytes is not\n    // one a reader can check.\n    let content = honouring_pinned_first_line(full_request, &content).map_or(content, |repaired| {\n        // Whether the repair applied is not recoverable from the finished plan,\n        // and the two outcomes it separates -- bytes taken from the prose, and\n        // bytes corrected to match a constraint stated elsewhere in the same\n        // request -- are exactly what a reader checking the plan needs to tell\n        // apart (default off; `FORMAL_AI_TRACE_REQUESTS=1`).\n        trace_route(\"general_change_plan\", \"repaired_pinned_first_line\");\n        repaired\n    });\n    if !safe_relative_path(&target) {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let response_language = language(request);\n    let intent = formalize_intent(request, response_language, None);\n    let verification_command = format!(\"cat {target}\");\n    let mut steps = vec![GeneralPlanStep {\n        capability: Capability::Write,\n        action: format!(\"append the composed plan to {PLAN_PATH}\"),\n        expected_evidence: format!(\"written plan event {}\", intent.impulse_id),\n        command: None,\n    }];\n    if let Some((_, command)) = &command_output {\n        let generation_command = format!(\"{command} > {}\", shell_quote(&target));\n        steps.push(GeneralPlanStep {\n            capability: Capability::Run,\n            action: command_plan_text(\n                \"general_plan_command_capture_action\",\n                response_language,\n                &target,\n            ),\n            expected_evidence: command_plan_text(\n                \"general_plan_command_output_evidence\",\n                response_language,\n                &target,\n            ),\n            command: Some(generation_command),\n        });\n    } else {\n        steps.push(GeneralPlanStep {\n            capability: Capability::Write,\n            action: format!(\"write the requested content to {target}\"),\n            expected_evidence: format!(\"workspace file {target}\"),\n            command: None,\n        });\n    }\n    steps.push(GeneralPlanStep {\n        capability: Capability::Run,\n        action: String::from(\"run the request-derived verification command\"),\n        expected_evidence: if command_output.is_some() {\n            command_plan_text(\n                \"general_plan_command_verification_evidence\",\n                response_language,\n                &target,\n            )\n        } else {\n            content.clone()\n        },\n        command: Some(verification_command.clone()),\n    });\n    Some(GeneralChangePlan {\n        id: stable_id(\n            \"general_change_plan\",\n            &format!(\n                \"{}:{target}:{content}:{}\",\n                intent.impulse_id,\n                command_output\n                    .as_ref()\n                    .map_or(\"\", |(_, command)| command.as_str())\n            ),\n        ),\n        mode: if command_output.is_some() {\n            GeneralPlanMode::CommandOutput\n        } else {\n            GeneralPlanMode::LiteralFile\n        },\n        goal: intent.source_text,\n        target,\n        content,\n        steps,\n        verification_command,\n        // The verification command observes the file the request named, not the\n        // plan record this run wrote, so the plan really is executed.\n        terminal_state: PlanTerminalState::Executed,\n    })\n}\nfn compose_repository_work_plan(request: &str) -> Option<GeneralChangePlan> {\n    let target = repository_work_reference(request)?;\n    if !mentions_bare_role(request, seed::ROLE_SOFTWARE_AUTHORING_ACTION) {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let response_language = language(request);\n    let intent = formalize_intent(request, response_language, None);\n    Some(GeneralChangePlan {\n        id: stable_id(\n            \"repository_work_item_plan\",\n            &format!(\"{}:{target}\", intent.impulse_id),\n        ),\n        mode: GeneralPlanMode::RepositoryWorkItem,\n        goal: intent.source_text,\n        target: target.clone(),\n        content: String::new(),\n        // A work item names an issue, not an artifact, so Bounding the span by the file clause alone reads\n/// across every sentence in between: \"Draft a handover memo containing the\n/// migration status, the outstanding blockers, and the on-call owner. Leave the\n/// memo in `handover/2026-q3.md`\" put the marker in the first sentence and the\n/// clause in the second, so the recovered payload ended with the words *Leave\n/// the memo* and the caller's memo opened by instructing them to leave it\n/// (issue #1066).\n///\n/// The clause bound still applies inside the sentence, because \"write the\n/// following: hello to `x.txt`\" states marker, payload and clause in one\n/// breath. Reading the payload at the scope\n/// shell routing reads at cut issue #918's minimal-core invariant in half at\n/// its semicolon.\nfn end_of_statement(request: &str, from: usize, limit: usize) -> usize {\n    let Some(sentence) = prose_sentences(request)\n        .into_iter()\n        .find(|sentence| sentence.span.contains(&from))\n    else {\n        return limit;\n    };\n    let says_more = request\n        .get(from..sentence.span.end)\n        .is_some_and(|tail| tail.chars().any(char::is_alphanumeric));\n    if says_more {\n        sentence.span.end.min(limit)\n    } else {\n        limit\n    }\n}\n/// Whether two write-request cues belong to one prose statement.\n///\n/// Literal-write roles are structural only inside the statement that relates\n/// them. Requiring the\n    // cue keeps an incidental dotted token out of the edit path, exactly as the\n    // write recogniser does.\n    let is_target_cue = |index: usize| target_cues.contains(&clean_cue_token(toks[index].text));\n    let is_action_cue = |index: usize| action_cues.contains(&clean_cue_token(toks[index].text));\n    let (file_index, target) = toks.iter().enumerate().find_map(|(index, token)| {\n        let cleaned = clean_path_token(token.text);\n        // A repository target may be named as a bare module or item — `source_links.rs`,\n        // `src/agentic_coding/source_links.rs:render_document`, or just\n        // `is_source_links_task` — in which case the workspace self-AST census\n        // (issue #673) resolves it to the module that actually declares it.\n        let resolved = resolve_census_target(cleaned);\n        let looks_like_file = looks_like_file_path(cleaned);\n        if resolved.is_none() && (!looks_like_file || !safe_relative_path(cleaned)) {\n            return None;\n        }\n        let prev_is_cue = index\n            .checked_sub(1)\n            .is_some_and(|previous| is_target_cue(previous) || is_action_cue(previous));\n        let next_is_cue =\n            (index + 1 < toks.len()) && (is_target_cue(index + 1) || is_action_cue(index + 1));\n        let target = resolved.map_or_else(|| cleaned.to_owned(), |census| census.module_path);\n        (prev_is_cue || next_is_cue).then_some((index, target))\n    })?;\n    // Extend the clause boundary left over any run of target cues so a multi-word\n    // file clause (\"в файле notes.txt\") is excluded from the replacement text in\n    // full, not just its innermost word.\n    let mut clause_start_index = file_index;\n    while clause_start_index > 0 && is_target_cue(clause_start_index - 1) {\n        clause_start_index -= 1;\n    }\n    let file_clause_start = toks[clause_start_index].start;\n    // The edit action opens the replacement clause; action_cues.contains(&clean_cue_token(token.text)))\n        })?;\n    let action_end = action.end;\n    let new_lead = toks.iter().find(|token| {\n        token.start >= action_end && answer.replace(\"{target}\", &plan.target);\n    answer.replace(\"{command}\", &plan.verification_command)\n}\n//! The resulting plan is data: it is serialized to\n//! Links Notation and written before execution, so the tool transcript is an\n//! append-only record of the decision that caused the change.\nuse super::planner::{Capability, trace_route};\nuse super::shell_command_policy::prose_sentences;\nuse super::write_request::{\n    bare_surfaces, clean_cue_token, clean_content, clean_path_token, cued_write_target,\n    first_action_cue_end, first_content_lead_end, first_prefix_lead_end,\n    honouring_pinned_first_line, looks_like_file_path, safe_relative_path, tokens,\n};\nuse crate::engine::stable_id;\nuse crate::intent_formalization::formalize_intent;\nuse crate::seed::{self, Slot};\nuse crate::self_ast_census::{self, CensusResolution};\nuse std::fmt::Write as _;\n/// Workspace-relative event-log artifact written before a general plan executes.\npub const PLAN_PATH: &str = \".formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino\";\nconst TARGET_PLACEHOLDER: &str = \"{target}\";\n/// What the bounded general planner can truthfully execute.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum GeneralPlanMode {\n    /// Write literal request content to a workspace-relative file.\n    LiteralFile,\n    /// Capture the output of an explicitly quoted command in a file.\n    CommandOutput,\n    /// Persist a referenced repository work item without fabricating a patch.\n    RepositoryWorkItem,\n}\nimpl GeneralPlanMode {\n    const fn slug(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            Self::LiteralFile => \"literal_file\",\n            Self::CommandOutput => \"command_output\",\n            Self::RepositoryWorkItem => \"repository_work_item\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n/// Where a composed plan can honestly end (issue #904).\n///\n/// A plan whose steps all operate on the plan record itself changes nothing the\n/// request named, and reading that record back verifies only that the run wrote\n/// it. struct GeneralChangePlan {\n    pub id: String,\n    pub mode: GeneralPlanMode,\n    pub goal: String,\n    pub target: String,\n    pub content: String,\n    pub steps: Vec<GeneralPlanStep>,\n    /// [`PlanTerminalState::PlannedNotExecuted`].\n    pub verification_command: String,\n    pub terminal_state: PlanTerminalState,\n}\nimpl GeneralChangePlan {\n    /// Render the plan shape consumed by the driver and documented by the meta fixture.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn links_notation(&self) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::from(\"general_change_plan\\n\");\n        field(&mut out, &self.goal);\n        field(&mut out, \"target\", &self.target);\n        for (index, step) in self.steps.iter().enumerate() {\n            let _ = writeln!(out, \"  step {}\", index + 1);\n Return the request after its first line-anchored multilingual objective marker.\n///\n/// This removes an agent-harness preamble. ),\n            command: Some(generation_command),\n        });\n    } else {\n        steps.push(GeneralPlanStep {\n            capability: Capability::Write,\n            action: format!(\"write the capability: Capability::Run,\n        action: String::from(\"run the request-derived verification command\"),\n        expected_evidence: if command_output.is_some() {\n &format!(\n                \"{}:{target}:{content}:{}\",\n                intent.impulse_id,\n                command_output\n                    .as_ref()\n                    .map_or(\"\", |(_, compose_repository_work_plan(request: &str) -> Option<GeneralChangePlan> {\n    let target = repository_work_reference(request)?;\n    if !mentions_bare_role(request, seed::ROLE_SOFTWARE_AUTHORING_ACTION) {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let response_language = language(request);\n    let intent = formalize_intent(request, response_language, None);\n    Some(GeneralChangePlan {\n        id: stable_id(\n            \"repository_work_item_plan\",\n            &format!(\"{}:{target}\", intent.impulse_id),\n        ),\n        mode:
