URL host/path\n/// segments are protocol identifiers, not natural-language routing phrases.\nfn repository_work_reference(request: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    request.split_whitespace().find_map(|token| {\n        let url = token.trim_matches(|character: char| {\n            matches!(\n                character,\n                '<' | '>' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | ',' | ';' | '.' | '\"' | '\\''\n            )\n        });\n        let path = url\n            .strip_prefix(\"https://github.com/\")\n            .or_else(|| url.strip_prefix(\"http://github.com/\"))?;\n        let segments: Vec<&str> = path.split('/').collect();\n        (segments.len() == 4\n            && !segments[0].is_empty()\n            && !segments[1].is_empty()\n            && matches!(segments[2], \"issues\" | \"pull\")\n            && segments[3]\n                .chars()\n                .all(|character| character.is_ascii_digit()))\n        .then(|| url.to_owned())\n    })\n}\n/// Recover a command-output file request from a structural, seed-backed frame.\n///\n/// The command must immediately follow a seed-defined run verb and be enclosed\n/// in single quotes, double quotes, or backticks. The suffix must name a\n/// seed-defined command-output reference, a file-write action, and a safe target\n/// introduced by a write target/destination cue. Requiring every element keeps\n/// an incidental quoted phrase or filename from becoming executable.\nfn parse_command_output_request(request: &str) -> Option<(String, String)> {\n    let toks = tokens(request);\n    let run_verbs = seed::terminal_command_vocabulary().run_verbs;\n    let actions = bare_surfaces(seed::ROLE_FILE_WRITE_ACTION_CUE);\n    let targets = bare_surfaces(seed::ROLE_FILE_WRITE_TARGET_CUE);\n    let destinations = bare_surfaces(seed::ROLE_FILE_WRITE_DESTINATION_CUE);\n    for run in toks\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|token| run_verbs.contains(&clean_cue_token(token.text)))\n    {\n        let tail = request.get(run.end..)?;\n        let leading = tail.len() - tail.trim_start().len();\n        let quoted = tail.get(leading..)?;\n        let quote = quoted.chars().next()?;\n        if !matches!(quote, '\\'' | '\"' | '`') {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let body = quoted.get(quote.len_utf8()..)?;\n        let Some(close) = body.find(quote) else {\n            continue;\n        };\n        let command = body.get(..close)?.trim();\n        if command.is_empty() || command.contains(['\\n', '\\r', '\\0']) {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let suffix_offset = run.end + leading + quote.len_utf8() + close + quote.len_utf8();\n        let suffix = request.get(suffix_offset..)?;\n        if !mentions_bare_role(suffix, seed::ROLE_FILE_WRITE_COMMAND_OUTPUT_REFERENCE) {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let suffix_tokens = tok…ix);\n        let has_write_action = suffix_tokens\n            .iter()\n            .any(|token| actions.contains(&clean_cue_token(token.text)));\n        if !has_write_action {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let target = suffix_tokens.iter().enumerate().find_map(|(index, token)| {\n            let cleaned = clean_path_token(token.text);\n            let looks_like_file = looks_like_file_path(cleaned);\n            let previous = index\n                .checked_sub(1)\n                .map(|position| &suffix_tokens[position])?;\n            let cue = clean_cue_token(previous.text);\n            (looks_like_file\n                && safe_relative_path(cleaned)\n                && (targets.contains(&cue) || destinations.contains(&cue)))\n            .then(|| cleaned.to_owned())\n        });\n        if let Some(target) = target {\n            return Some((target, command.to_owned()));\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\nfn mentions_bare_role(text: &str, role: &str) -> bool {\n    let lower = text.to_lowercase();\n    seed::lexicon()\n        .role_word_forms(role)\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|form| form.slot() == Slot::Bare)\n        .any(|form| {\n            let needle = form.text.to_lowercase();\n            let Some(start) = lower.find(&needle) else {\n                return false;\n            };\n            if !needle.is_ascii() {\n                return true;\n            }\n            let end = start + needle.len();\n            let before_ok = start == 0\n                || lower[..start]\n                    .chars()\n                    .next_back()\n                    .is_some_and(|character| !character.is_alphanumeric());\n            let after_ok = end == lower.len()\n                || lower[end..]\n                    .chars()\n                    .next()\n                    .is_some_and(|character| !character.is_alphanumeric());\n            before_ok && after_ok\n        })\n}\nfn shell_quote(value: &str) -> String {\n    format!(\"'{}'\", value.replace('\\'', \"'\\\\''\"))\n}\nfn command_plan_text(intent: &str, language: &str, target: &str) -> String {\n    seed::localized_response(intent, language)\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| intent.to_owned())\n        .replace(TARGET_PLACEHOLDER, target)\n}\n/// Whether `lower` (an already-lowercased request) is a file **write / create**\n/// intent — a write verb applied to something file-shaped. This is the single\n/// signal the router uses to keep a file-creation request from ever being\n/// misrouted to the file-read recipe (issue #681): a request to *produce* a file\n/// is a write, never a read of the not-yet-existing target.\n///\n/// This is intentionally the same structural parse used to compose the eventual\n/// write plan. A request is classified as a write only when the seed-defined\n/// action/target/content roles yield a safe target and non-empty payload. One\n/// parser for classification and composition cannot drift into claiming an\n/// operation that the planner is unable to execute.\n#[must_use]\npub(crate) fn has_file_write_intent(lower: &str) -> bool {\n    parse_write_request(lower).is_some()\n}\n/// Whether a request explicitly marks its recovered payload as authoritative\n/// literal bytes rather than a description of another workspace operation.\n///\n/// The marker is seed-backed and multilingual. Requiring both the narrow marker\n/// role and a successfully composed literal-file plan prevents arbitrary prose\n/// containing \"exactly\" from changing planner precedence.\npub(super) fn has_authoritative_literal_write(request: &str) -> bool {\n    let normalized = request.to_lowercase();\n    first_prefix_lead_end(\n        &normalized,\n        seed::ROLE_FILE_WRITE_AUTHORITATIVE_CONTENT_LEAD,\n    )\n    .is_some()\n        && compose_general_change_plan(request)\n            .is_some_and(|plan| plan.mode == GeneralPlanMode::LiteralFile)\n}\n/// Recover the `(target, content)` of a write request from its wording.\n///\n/// The recogniser is entirely seed-driven (issue #680). It locates the target\n/// file by a `file_write_target_cue`/`file_write_destination_cue` that directly\n/// precedes a file-looking, safe relative path, then recovers the content two\n/// ways:\n///\n/// * **Marker-led** — a `file_write_content_lead` phrase (\"containing\", \"with\n///   the following\", …) introduces the payload. The content is the span after\n///   the marker (when the file precedes it) or the span between the marker and\n///   the file clause (when the content precedes the file).\n/// * **Destination-led** — the \"write CONTENT to FILE\" shape, where a\n///   `file_write_action_cue` opens the request and a *destination* cue (not a\n///   positional target cue) routes the preceding span into the file.\n/// * **Action-led** — the \"write FILE saying CONTENT\" shape, where a\n///   `file_write_action_cue` (\"write\"/\"create\"/\"save\"/…) directly names the file\n///   and a content-lead marker introduces the payload after it. An action cue\n///   licenses the file just like a target cue, but only marker-led content is\n///   accepted for it, so a bare \"create app.rs\" (no content) still falls through\n///   to the ordinary solver rather than fabricating an empty file.\n///\n/// Both byte offsets index the lowercased copy, which is byte-length preserving\n/// for en/ru/hi/zh, so the same offsets slice the original request and the\n/// recovered content keeps its case and punctuation.\nfn parse_write_request(request: &str) -> Option<(String, String)> {\n    let lowered = request.to_lowercase();\n    let toks = tokens(request);\n    let dest_cues = bare_surfaces(seed::ROLE_FILE_WRITE_DESTINATION_CUE);\n    let (file_index, target) = cued_write_target(&toks)?;\n    let cue = &toks[file_index - 1];\n    let clause_start = cue.start;\n    let cue_is_destination = dest_cues.contains(&clean_cue_token(cue.text));\n    // Marker-led content. The payload sits after the marker, bounded by the file\n    // clause when the marker comes first (\"write the following: hello to x.txt\")\n    // and running to the end when the clause comes first (\"store file x.txt\n    // containing hello\").\n    //\n    // A marker that *precedes* the clause additionally needs a write verb, which\n    // is the same rule the destination-led and assignment-shaped branches below\n    // already apply — without it a read request whose object happens to be a\n    // content-lead surface claims a write. The issue-#671 matrix caught\n    // `show me the contents of the file beta.md` planning\n    // `write(beta.md, \"of the\")`, destroying the fixture it was asked to read.\n    // A marker inside a sentence that specifies a document to compose introduces\n    // that document's structure, not its bytes; see\n    // [`super::note_composition::composed_document_specification_span`]. Reading\n    // it as a literal payload is what wrote \"the selected tree level, node\n    // outcomes, test results, and session id.\" into the ladder's final proof\n    // file (issue #1066), and it claimed the request too, so the note the caller\n    // asked for was never composed.\n    let specification = super::note_composition::composed_document_specification_span(request);\n    if let Some((_, marker_end)) = first_content_lead_end(&lowered)\n        && !specification.is_some_and(|span| span.contains(&marker_end))\n        && positions_share_statement(request, marker_end, clause_start)\n    {\n        let marker_leads = marker_end <= clause_start;\n        let marker_span = if marker_leads {\n            request.get(marker_end..end_of_statement(request, marker_end, clause_start))\n        } else {\n            request.get(marker_end..end_of_statement(request, marker_end, request.len()))\n        };\n        if (!marker_leads || first_action_cue_end(&toks).is_some())\n            && let Some(content) = marker_span\n                .and_then(clean_content)\n                .filter(|content| is_literal_content(content))\n            {\n                return Some((target, content));\n            }\n    }\n    let content_span = if cue_is_destination {\n        let action_end = first_action_cue_end(&toks)?;\n        (action_end <= clause_start\n            && positions_share_statement(request, action_end, clause_start))\n        .then(|| request.get(action_end..clause_start))?\n    } else if let Some(value_lead) = toks\n        .iter()\n        .skip(file_index + 1)\n        .find(|token| dest_cues.contains(&clean_cue_token(token.text)))\n    {\n        // Assignment shape: \"set the contents of FILE to VALUE\". The target\n        // cue identifies the file object and a following destination cue\n        // introduces its literal value. Requiring a write action before the\n        // file keeps an unrelated \"contents of FILE\" read request out.\n        let action_end = first_action_cue_end(&toks)?;\n        (action_end <= clause_start\n            && positions_share_statement(request, action_end, clause_start)\n            && positions_share_statement(request, clause_start, value_lead.start))\n        .then(|| request.get(value_lead.end..))?\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n    let content = clean_content(content_span?)?;\n    // A recovered payload that is *only* a non-referential subject (\"save it to\n    // FILE\", \"write this to FILE\") names no literal content — the pronoun points\n    // back at content the request expects the recipe to still compose. Treating\n    // it as a literal write both fabricates the wrong file (the string \"it\") and\n    // steals the request from the keyword recipe that would author the real\n    // artifact, so fall through instead (issue #663).\n    //\n    // The same is true of a payload that names the *work product* rather than\n    // supplying it: \"save the answer to FILE\" states where an answer goes, not\n    // what it says (issue #1066).\n    if is_non_referential_content(&content)\n        || names_deferred_work_product(&content)\n        || !is_literal_content(&content)\n    {\n        return None;\n    }\n    Some((target, content))\n}\n/// Where the statement that begins at `from` ends, never past `limit`.\n///\n/// A literal payload is something the request *states*, and a statement ends\n/// where its sentence does. Bounding the span by the file clause alone reads\n/// across every sentence in between: \"Draft a handover memo containing the\n/// migration status, the outstanding blockers, and the on-call owner. Leave the\n/// memo in `handover/2026-q3.md`\" put the marker in the first sentence and the\n/// clause in the second, so the recovered payload ended with the words *Leave\n/// the memo* and the caller's memo opened by instructing them to leave it\n/// (issue #1066).\n///\n/// The clause bound still applies inside the sentence, because \"write the\n/// following: hello to `x.txt`\" states marker, payload and clause in one\n/// breath. This only refuses to look further than the sentence the marker is in.\n///\n/// A marker that says nothing more on its own line is the exception, because\n/// there the payload is a *block* rather than a phrase: \"Create file\n/// `rules.lino` containing\\n<three lines of lino>\" leaves the marker with an\n/// empty tail, and a newline ends a sentence, so the sentence bound would\n/// recover nothing at all. When the marker's own line has no word left on it,\n/// the statement is the block that follows and runs to `limit`, which is what\n/// this route always did for block payloads.\n///\n/// The sentence is the one *prose* reads, so a semicolon inside the payload\n/// joins its two halves instead of ending it. Reading the payload at the scope\n/// shell routing reads at cut issue #918's minimal-core invariant in half at\n/// its semicolon.\nfn end_of_statement(request: &str, from: usize, limit: usize) -> usize {\n    let Some(sentence) = prose_sentences(request)\n        .into_iter()\n        .find(|sentence| sentence.span.contains(&from))\n    else {\n        return limit;\n    };\n    let says_more = request\n        .get(from..sentence.span.end)\n        .is_some_and(|tail| tail.chars().any(char::is_alphanumeric));\n    if says_more {\n        sentence.span.end.min(limit)\n    } else {\n        limit\n    }\n}\n/// Whether two write-request cues belong to one prose statement.\n///\n/// Literal-write roles are structural only inside the statement that relates\n/// them. Without this check, a content lead in one issue-description paragraph\n/// can pair with an incidental file-shaped token in a later paragraph and turn\n/// repository policy prose into an executable write (issue #1069).\n///\n/// [`end_of_statement`] deliberately lets a marker-only line introduce the\n/// block below it. Reusing that boundary here preserves that supported block\n/// shape while rejecting ordinary completed sentences between the two cues.\nfn positions_share_statement(request: &str, left: usize, right: usize) -> bool {\n    let (from, limit) = if left <= right {\n        (left, right)\n    } else {\n        (right, left)\n    };\n    from == limit || end_of_statement(request, from, limit) == limit\n}\n/// Whether a recovered payload says anything at all. A span of nothing but\n/// punctuation is what a mis-parse leaves behind — the `opencode` leg of the\n/// issue-#671 matrix recovered a single `\"`, the tail of a quoted prompt after\n/// its trailing content-lead marker — and writing it would replace real file\n/// bytes with a stray delimiter.\nfn is_literal_content(content: &str) -> bool {\n    content.chars().any(char::is_alphanumeric)\n}\n/// Whether a recovered write payload is nothing but a non-referential subject —\n/// a bare pronoun/function word (\"it\", \"this\", \"that\", …) that refers back to\n/// context rather than naming literal content. The surfaces carry the\n/// [`seed::ROLE_NON_REFERENTIAL_SUBJECT`] role; only whole-word\n/// ([`Slot::Bare`]) forms are rejected, so legitimate content that merely\n/// *begins* with such a word (\"to be or not to be\") is still accepted.\nfn is_non_referential_content(content: &str) -> bool {\n    let lower = content.to_lowercase();\n    seed::lexicon()\n        .role_word_forms(seed::ROLE_NON_REFERENTIAL_SUBJECT)\n        .iter()\n        .any(|form| form.slot() == Slot::Bare && lower == form.text)\n}\n/// Whether a recovered write payload names the result of work the same request\n/// asks for, instead of supplying bytes (issue #1066).\n///\n/// \"Save the answer to `out/e.md`\" and \"leave observable evidence to\n/// `out/e.md`\" have the destination-led shape of a literal write -- a write\n/// verb, a span, a destination cue, a path -- and supply no literal. Taking the\n/// span at face value wrote the words *the answer* into the file and, worse,\n/// claimed the request as finished, so the investigation that would have\n/// produced the real bytes never ran.\n///\n/// The surfaces carry [`seed::ROLE_FILE_WRITE_DEFERRED_CONTENT_REFERENCE`] as\n/// [`Slot::Suffix`] forms, because the head noun is what defers and the\n/// modifiers in front of it (\"observable\", \"final\") are the caller's, not the\n/// lexicon's.\n///\n/// Deliberately not applied to marker-led content. \"Create `a.txt` containing 42\n/// is the answer\" states, with the marker, that the span *is* the payload; only\n/// the shapes that infer a payload from position need the check.\nfn names_deferred_work_product(content: &str) -> bool {\n    let lower = content.to_lowercase();\n    seed::lexicon()\n        .role_word_forms(seed::ROLE_FILE_WRITE_DEFERRED_CONTENT_REFERENCE)\n        .iter()\n        .any(|form| match form.slot() {\n            Slot::Bare => lower == form.text,\n            Slot::Suffix => ends_with_head_noun(&lower, form.after_slot().trim_start()),\n            Slot::Prefix | Slot::Circumfix => false,\n        })\n}\n/// Whether `content` ends with `noun` standing as its own word.\n///\n/// English and Russian separate a head noun from its modifiers with a space, so\n/// the character before the match settles it. Chinese writes the same phrase\n/// with no separator at all, which is why the boundary is stated as \"not an\n/// ASCII alphanumeric\" rather than \"whitespace\": demanding a space would never\n/// match 结论, and demanding nothing would match the tail of an unrelated\n/// English word.\nfn ends_with_head_noun(content: &str, noun: &str) -> bool {\n    !noun.is_empty()\n        && content.strip_suffix(noun).is_some_and(|before| {\n            before\n                .chars()\n                .next_back()\n                .is_none_or(|character| !character.is_ascii_alphanumeric())\n        })\n}\n/// Resolve an edit target named in a request through the workspace self-AST\n/// census (issue #673).\n///\n/// Before the census existed, the planner could only edit a file the request spelt\n/// out in full, and its own self-inspection was pinned to a single hardcoded module\n/// (`src/agentic_coding/planner.rs`). The census itself fails closed on anything ambiguous.\n#[must_use]\npub fn resolve_census_target(reference: &str) -> Option<CensusResolution> {\n    let addresses_workspace =\n        reference.contains('/') || (reference.contains(':') && !reference.contains(\"://\"));\n    if !addresses_workspace {\n        return None;\n    }\n    self_ast_census::workspace().resolve(reference)\n}\n/// Recover the `(target, old, new)` of a file-edit request from its wording\n/// (issue #680).\n///\n/// The recogniser is entirely seed-driven. It locates the target file by a\n/// [`ROLE_FILE_EDIT_TARGET_CUE`](seed::ROLE_FILE_EDIT_TARGET_CUE) (\"in\", \"within\",\n/// \"of\", \"file\", …) that directly precedes a file-looking, safe relative path,\n/// finds the leftmost\n/// [`ROLE_FILE_EDIT_ACTION_CUE`](seed::ROLE_FILE_EDIT_ACTION_CUE) (\"change\",\n/// \"replace\", \"edit\", …), then the first\n/// [`ROLE_FILE_EDIT_NEW_LEAD_CUE`](seed::ROLE_FILE_EDIT_NEW_LEAD_CUE) (\"to\",\n/// \"with\", \"into\", …) after it. The *old* text is the span between the action and\n/// the new-lead; the *new* text is the span after the new-lead, bounded by the\n/// file clause when the file follows the replacement (the \"replace OLD with NEW in\n/// FILE\" shape) or running to the end when the file was named first (the \"in FILE,\n/// change OLD to NEW\" shape).\n///\n/// Returns [`None`] unless a target file, an action cue, a new-lead, and non-empty\n/// old and new spans are all present — and unless the file clause sits *outside*\n/// the replaced span — so ambiguous or non-edit requests fall through to the\n/// ordinary solver rather than fabricating an edit.\n///\n/// Byte offsets index the original request directly (the cue matching lowercases\n/// per token, which is byte-length preserving for en/ru/hi/zh), so the recovered\n/// old/new text keeps its original case and punctuation.\n#[must_use]\npub fn compose_edit_request(request: &str) -> Option<(String, String, String)> {\n    let toks = tokens(request);\n    let action_cues = bare_surfaces(seed::ROLE_FILE_EDIT_ACTION_CUE);\n    let new_leads = bare_surfaces(seed::ROLE_FILE_EDIT_NEW_LEAD_CUE);\n    let target_cues = bare_surfaces(seed::ROLE_FILE_EDIT_TARGET_CUE);\n    // The target file: the first safe, file-looking token that sits directly beside\n    // a target cue — before it in prepositional languages (\"in notes.txt\") or after\n    // it in postpositional ones (\"doc.txt में\", \"the report.md file\"). Failure-driven recursive task execution.\n     2\t//!\n     3\t//! The meta core already describes a bounded task tree. This module supplies the\n     4\t//! missing execution back-edge: try the parent, descend only after failure,\n     5\t//! extend the tool at an irreducible unsupported leaf, then climb back up and\n     6\t//! validate the parent after every child passes.\n     7\t//!\n     8\t//! A caller-provided tree is not the only source of children. A task that fails\n     9\t//! with no children left to try is asked to *split itself* through\n    10\t//! [`TaskExecutor::split`], and the resulting sub-tasks are executed by the same\n    11\t//! protocol. That is what makes the recursion failure-driven rather than\n    12\t//! plan-driven: the decomposition a run needs is discovered from the failure it\n    13\t//! actually hit, and splitting continues until either a level passes or the\n    14\t//! task is irreducible -- which is exactly when extending the tool is the\n    15\t//! honest move. [`crate::task_decomposition::SplittingExecutor`] wires the\n    16\t//! repository's real splitter into this hook.\n    17\t//!\n    18\t//! Termination is structural, not hopeful. A split may only run while the\n    19\t//! node's split depth is below the bound, a child that repeats its parent's\n    20\t//! identity or goal is discarded, and a node whose split yields nothing usable\n    21\t//! is treated as irreducible. So every path through the protocol reaches a\n    22\t//! terminal state in a bounded number of attempts.\n    23\t\n    24\t/// One executable task in a caller-provided decomposition tree.\n    25\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\n    26\tpub struct RecursiveTask {\n    27\t    /// Stable task identity used by evidence and tests.\n    28\t    pub id: String,\n    29\t    /// Natural-language task handed to the executor.\n    30\t    pub goal: String,\n    31\t    /// Smaller tasks, in composition order.\n    32\t    pub children: Vec<Self>,\n    33\t}\n    34\t\n    35\timpl RecursiveTask {\n    36\t    /// Construct an elementary task.\n    37\t    #[must_use]\n    38\t    pub fn leaf(id: impl Into<String>, goal: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n    39\t        Self {\n    40\t            id: id.into(),\n    41\t            goal: goal.into(),\n    42\t            children: Vec::new(),\n    43\t        }\n    44\t    }\n    45\t\n    46\t    /// Construct a task with an explicit, reviewable decomposition.\n    47\t    #[must_use]\n    48\t    pub fn branch(id: impl Into<String>, goal: impl Into<String>, children: Vec<Self>) -> Self {\n    49\t        Self {\n    50\t            id: id.into(),\n    51\t            goal: goal.into(),\n    52\t            children,\n    53\t        }\n    54\t    }\n    55\t}\n    56\t\n    57\t/// Result of one test-backed attempt by the task executor.\n    58\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\n    59\tpub struct TaskAttempt {\n    60\t    /// Whether the task's acceptance test passed.\n    61\t    pub passed: bool,\n    62\t    /// Captured test/session evidence or the concrete failure.\n    63\t    pub evidence: String,\n    64\t}\n    65\t\n    66\timpl TaskAttempt {\n    67\t    /// Record a passing attempt.\n    68\t    #[must_use]\n    69\t    pub fn passed(evidence: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n    70\t        Self {\n    71\t            passed: true,\n    72\t            evidence: evidence.into(),\n    73\t        }\n    74\t    }\n    75\t\n    76\t    /// Record a failing attempt.\n    77\t    #[must_use]\n    78\t    pub fn failed(evidence: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n    79\t        Self {\n    80\t            passed: false,\n    81\t            evidence: evidence.into(),\n    82\t        }\n    83\t    }\n    84\t}\n    85\t\n    86\t/// Tool boundary used by the recursive controller.\n    87\t///\n    88\t/// `attempt` must run the task and its acceptance test. `split` is called first\n    89\t/// for a failed task with no children, and may return smaller tasks derived\n    90\t/// from the failure; returning an empty list declares the task irreducible.\n    91\t/// `extend_for` is called only for a failed *irreducible* task; returning\n    92\t/// `true` promises that the tool was extended and the same leaf should be\n    93\t/// retried once. `retry_after_children` validates a parent after all of its\n    94\t/// child effects have been composed; its default performs another ordinary\n    95\t/// attempt, while executors with an independent verifier may accept the\n    96\t/// composition without risking another mutating tool call.\n    97\tpub trait TaskExecutor {\n    98\t    /// Attempt one task and capture its evidence.\n    99\t    fn attempt(&mut self, task: &RecursiveTask) -> TaskAttempt;\n   100\t\n   101\t    /// Extend the general tool for a failed elementary task.\n   102\t    fn extend_for(&mut self, task: &RecursiveTask, failure: &TaskAttempt) -> bool;\n   103\t\n   104\t    /// Split a failed childless task into smaller ones, from its failure.\n   105\t    ///\n   106\t    /// `split_depth` is how many splits already happened above this node, so an\n   107\t    /// implementation can spend a shrinking budget; the controller enforces its\n   108\t    /// own bound regardless. The default refuses to split, which is the honest\n   109\t    /// answer for an executor that has no splitter: such a task goes straight\n   110\t    /// to [`TaskExecutor::extend_for`], exactly as before this hook existed.\n   111\t    fn split(\n   112\t        &mut self,\n   113\t        _task: &RecursiveTask,\n   114\t        _failure: &TaskAttempt,\n   115\t        _split_depth: u8,\n   116\t    ) -> Vec<RecursiveTask> {\n   117\t        Vec::new()\n   118\t    }\n   119\t\n   120\t    /// Validate a parent after every child passed and its effects were composed.\n   121\t    ///\n   122\t    /// The default preserves the original climb-back-up protocol. Executors\n   123\t    /// with a trustworthy acceptance test can override this to verify the\n   124\t    /// composition before deciding whether another mutating attempt is needed.\n   125\t    fn retry_after_children(&mut self, task: &RecursiveTask) -> TaskAttempt {\n   126\t        self.attempt(task)\n   127\t    }\n   128\t}\n   129\t\n   130\t/// Terminal state of one executed task node.\n   131\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\n   132\tpub enum RecursiveExecution {\n   133\t    /// Its test passed, directly or after recursion.\n   134\t    Passed,\n   135\t    /// It remained unsolved after the bounded recovery protocol.\n   136\t    Blocked,\n   137\t}\n   138\t\n   139\t/// Complete evidence tree for a failure-driven recursive run.\n   140\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\n   141\tpub struct RecursiveRun {\n   142\t    /// Task represented by this node.\n   143\t    pub task: RecursiveTask,\n   144\t    /// Attempts made at this level, in time order.\n   145\t    pub attempts: Vec<TaskAttempt>,\n   146\t    /// Executed child runs, in composition order.\n   147\t    pub children: Vec<Self>,\n   148\t    /// Whether an elementary failure caused a tool extension.\n   149\t    pub extension_applied: bool,\n   150\t    /// Whether this node's children were produced by splitting its own failure\n   151\t    /// rather than supplied by the caller's tree.\n   152\t    pub split_applied: bool,\n   153\t    /// Terminal state.\n   154\t    pub status: RecursiveExecution,\n   155\t}\n   156\t\n   157\timpl RecursiveRun {\n   158\t    /// Whether this node passed its acceptance test.\n   159\t    #[must_use]\n   160\t    pub const fn is_passed(&self) -> bool {\n   161\t        matches!(self.status, RecursiveExecution::Passed)\n   162\t    }\n   163\t\n   164\t    /// Count recursively executed leaves.\n   165\t    #[must_use]\n   166\t    pub fn executed_leaf_count(&self) -> usize {\n   167\t        if self.children.is_empty() {\n   168\t            1\n   169\t        } else {\n   170\t            self.children.iter().map(Self::executed_leaf_count).sum()\n   171\t        }\n   172\t    }\n   173\t\n   174\t    /// How deep the failure-driven splitting went below this node.\n   175\t    ///\n   176\t    /// Zero when nothing was split, so a plan-driven run reports zero however\n   177\t    /// deep the caller's tree was.\n   178\t    #[must_use]\n   179\t    pub fn split_depth_reached(&self) -> u8 {\n   180\t        let below = self\n   181\t            .children\n   182\t            .iter()\n   183\t            .map(Self::split_depth_reached)\n   184\t            .max()\n   185\t            .unwrap_or(0);\n   186\t        below.saturating_add(u8::from(self.split_applied))\n   187\t    }\n   188\t\n   189\t    /// Every node that ended [`RecursiveExecution::Blocked`] with no children,\n   190\t    /// in execution order.\n   191\t    ///\n   192\t    /// These are the irreducible tasks: splitting could not shrink them and the\n   193\t    /// tool could not be extended for them, so they are precisely the places\n   194\t    /// where new capability has to be added.\n   195\t    #[must_use]\n   196\t    pub fn blocked_leaves(&self) -> Vec<&Self> {\n   197\t        if self.children.is_empty() {\n   198\t            return if self.is_passed() {\n   199\t                Vec::new()\n   200\t            } else {\n   201\t                vec![self]\n   202\t            };\n   203\t        }\n   204\t        self.children\n   205\t            .iter()\n   206\t            .flat_map(Self::blocked_leaves)\n   207\t            .collect()\n   208\t    }\n   209\t}\n   210\t\n   211\t/// How many times a failure may be split before the controller stops asking.\n   212\t///\n   213\t/// A splitter that keeps producing marginally different children would\n   214\t/// otherwise recurse without end. Four levels is more than the repository's own\n   215\t/// decomposition artifacts reach and still terminates in bounded work.\n   216\tpub const DEFAULT_SPLIT_DEPTH_BOUND: u8 = 4;\n   217\t\n   218\t/// Execute the shrink-on-failure protocol over `root`.\n   219\t///\n   220\t/// Every node is attempted before descent. A failed branch executes its smaller\n   221\t/// children and is validated only if all of them pass. A failed node with no\n   222\t/// children is asked to split itself from its own failure; the children it\n   223\t/// yields are executed by this same protocol and the node is validated when\n   224\t/// they all pass. Only a node that cannot be split -- an irreducible task --\n   225\t/// gets one extension opportunity and one retry, which keeps execution bounded.\n   226\t///\n   227\t/// Splitting stops at [`DEFAULT_SPLIT_DEPTH_BOUND`]; use\n   228\t/// [`solve_recursively_within`] to choose another bound.\n   229\t#[must_use]\n   230\tpub fn solve_recursively<E: TaskExecutor>(root: &RecursiveTask, Grey, not red. No failure notification, no entry in the failed-runs filter.  That is why issue #977 describes the pipeline as `cancelled` rather than `failing`. [2026-09-02T21:47:05.480Z] [STDERR] Title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
[2026-09-02T21:47:05.480Z] [STDERR] Authors: Guanzhi Wang, Yuqi Xie, Yunfan Jiang, Ajay Mandlekar, Chaowei Xiao, Yuke Zhu, Linxi Fan, Anima Anandkumar
[2026-09-02T21:47:05.480Z] [STDERR] Date: Thu May 25 17:46:38 2023
[2026-09-02T21:47:05.480Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T21:47:05.480Z] [STDERR] We introduce Voyager, the first LLM-powered embodied lifelong learning agent in Minecraft that continuously explores the world, acquires diverse skills, and makes novel discoveries without human intervention. Voyager consists of three key components: 1) an automatic curriculum that maximizes exploration, 2) an ever-growing skill library of executable code for storing and retrieving complex behaviors, and 3) a new iterative prompting mechanism that incorporates environment feedback, execution errors, and self-verification for program improvement. Voyager interacts with GPT-4 via blackbox queries, which bypasses the need for model parameter fine-tuning. The skills developed by Voyager are temporally extended, interpretable, and compositional, which compounds the agent's abilities rapidly and alleviates catastrophic forgetting. Empirically, Voyager shows strong in-context lifelong learning capability and exhibits exceptional proficiency in playing Minecraft. It obtains 3.3x more unique items, travels 2.3x longer distances, and unlocks key tech tree milestones up to 15.3x faster than prior SOTA. Voyager is able to utilize the learned skill library in a new Minecraft world to solve novel tasks from scratch, while other techniques struggle to generalize.

[2026-09-02T21:47:11.944Z] [STDERR] Title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
[2026-09-02T21:47:11.944Z] [STDERR] Authors: Aman Madaan, Niket Tandon, Prakhar Gupta, Skyler Hallinan, Luyu Gao, Sarah Wiegreffe, Uri Alon, Nouha Dziri, Shrimai Prabhumoye, Yiming Yang, Shashank Gupta, Bodhisattwa Prasad Majumder, Katherine Hermann, Sean Welleck, Amir Yazdanbakhsh, Peter Clark
[2026-09-02T21:47:11.944Z] [STDERR] Date: Thu Mar 30 18:30:01 2023
[2026-09-02T21:47:11.944Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T21:47:11.944Z] [STDERR] Like humans, large language models (LLMs) do not always generate the best output on their first try. Motivated by how humans refine their written text, we introduce Self-Refine, an approach for improving initial outputs from LLMs through iterative feedback and refinement. The main idea is to generate an initial output using an LLMs; then, the same LLMs provides feedback for its output and uses it to refine itself, iteratively. Self-Refine does not require any supervised training data, additional training, or reinforcement learning, and instead uses a single LLM as the generator, refiner, and feedback provider. We evaluate Self-Refine across 7 diverse tasks, ranging from dialog response generation to mathematical reasoning, using state-of-the-art (GPT-3.5, ChatGPT, and GPT-4) LLMs. Across all evaluated tasks, outputs generated with Self-Refine are preferred by humans and automatic metrics over those generated with the same LLM using conventional one-step generation, improving by ~20% absolute on average in task performance. .rposition(|message| message.role.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"user\"))\n        .map_or(0, |index| index + 1);\n    messages\n        .iter()\n        .enumerate()\n        .skip(current_turn)\n Failure-driven recursive task execution.\n//!\n//! The meta core already describes a bounded task tree. This module supplies the\n//! missing execution back-edge: try the parent, descend only after failure,\n//! extend the tool at an irreducible unsupported leaf, then climb back up and\n//! validate the parent after every child passes.\n//!\n//! A caller-provided tree is not the only source of children. A task that fails\n//! with no children left to try is asked to *split itself* through\n//! [`TaskExecutor::split`], and the resulting sub-tasks are executed by the same\n//! protocol. That is what makes the recursion failure-driven rather than\n//! plan-driven: the decomposition a run needs is discovered from the failure it\n//! actually hit, and splitting continues until either a level passes or the\n//! task is irreducible -- which is exactly when extending the tool is the\n//! honest move. [`crate::task_decomposition::SplittingExecutor`] wires the\n//! repository's real splitter into this hook.\n//!\n//! Termination is structural, not hopeful. A split may only run while the\n//! node's split depth is below the bound, a child that repeats its parent's\n//! identity or goal is discarded, and a node whose split yields nothing usable\n//! is treated as irreducible. So every path through the protocol reaches a\n//! terminal state in a bounded number of attempts.\n\n/// One executable task in a caller-provided decomposition tree.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct RecursiveTask {\n    /// Stable task identity used by evidence and tests.\n    pub id: String,\n    /// Natural-language task handed to the executor.\n    pub goal: String,\n    /// Smaller tasks, in composition order.\n    pub children: Vec<Self>,\n}\n\nimpl RecursiveTask {\n    /// Construct an elementary task.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn leaf(id: impl Into<String>, goal: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            id: id.into(),\n            goal: goal.into(),\n            children: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Construct a task with an explicit, reviewable decomposition.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn branch(id: impl Into<String>, goal: impl Into<String>, children: Vec<Self>) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            id: id.into(),\n            goal: goal.into(),\n            children,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Result of one test-backed attempt by the task executor.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct TaskAttempt {\n    /// Whether the task's acceptance test passed.\n    pub passed: bool,\n    /// Captured test/session evidence or the concrete failure.\n    pub evidence: String,\n}\n\nimpl TaskAttempt {\n    /// Record a passing attempt.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn passed(evidence: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            passed: true,\n            evidence: evidence.into(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record a failing attempt.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn failed(evidence: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            passed: false,\n            evidence: evidence.into(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Tool boundary used by the recursive controller.\n///\n/// `attempt` must run the task and its acceptance test. `split` is called first\n/// for a failed task with no children, and may return smaller tasks derived\n/// from the failure; returning an empty list declares the task irreducible.\n/// `extend_for` is called only for a failed *irreducible* task; returning\n/// `true` promises that the tool was extended and the same leaf should be\n/// retried once. `retry_after_children` validates a parent after all of its\n/// child effects have been composed; its default performs another ordinary\n/// attempt, while executors with an independent verifier may accept the\n/// composition without risking another mutating tool call.\npub trait TaskExecutor {\n    /// Attempt one task and capture its evidence.\n    fn attempt(&mut self, task: &RecursiveTask) -> TaskAttempt;\n\n    /// Extend the general tool for a failed elementary task.\n    fn extend_for(&mut self, task: &RecursiveTask, failure: &TaskAttempt) -> bool;\n\n    /// Split a failed childless task into smaller ones, from its failure.\n    ///\n    /// `split_depth` is how many splits already happened above this node, so an\n    /// implementation can spend a shrinking budget; the controller enforces its\n    /// own bound regardless. The default refuses to split, which is the honest\n    /// answer for an executor that has no splitter: such a task goes straight\n    /// to [`TaskExecutor::extend_for`], exactly as before this hook existed.\n    fn split(\n        &mut self,\n        _task: &RecursiveTask,\n        _failure: &TaskAttempt,\n        _split_depth: u8,\n    ) -> Vec<RecursiveTask> {\n        Vec::new()\n    }\n\n    /// Validate a parent after every child passed and its effects were composed.\n    ///\n    /// The default preserves the original climb-back-up protocol. Executors\n    /// with a trustworthy acceptance test can override this to verify the\n    /// composition before deciding whether another mutating attempt is needed.\n    fn retry_after_children(&mut self, task: &RecursiveTask) -> TaskAttempt {\n        self.attempt(task)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Terminal state of one executed task node.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum RecursiveExecution {\n    /// Its test passed, directly or after recursion.\n    Passed,\n    /// It remained unsolved after the bounded recovery protocol.\n    Blocked,\n}\n\n/// Complete evidence tree for a failure-driven recursive run.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct RecursiveRun {\n    /// Task represented by this node.\n    pub task: RecursiveTask,\n    /// Attempts made at this level, in time order.\n    pub attempts: Vec<TaskAttempt>,\n    /// Executed child runs, in composition order.\n    pub children: Vec<Self>,\n    /// Whether an elementary failure caused a tool extension.\n    pub extension_applied: bool,\n    /// Whether this node's children were produced by splitting its own failure\n    /// rather than supplied by the caller's tree.\n    pub split_applied: bool,\n    /// Terminal state.\n    pub status: RecursiveExecution,\n}\n\nimpl RecursiveRun {\n    /// Whether this node passed its acceptance test.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub const fn is_passed(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self.status, RecursiveExecution::Passed)\n    }\n\n    /// Count recursively executed leaves.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn executed_leaf_count(&self) -> usize {\n        if self.children.is_empty() {\n            1\n        } else {\n            self.children.iter().map(Self::executed_leaf_count).sum()\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// How deep the failure-driven splitting went below this node.\n    ///\n    /// Zero when nothing was split, so a plan-driven run reports zero however\n    /// deep the caller's tree was.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn split_depth_reached(&self) -> u8 {\n        let below = self\n            .children\n            .iter()\n            .map(Self::split_depth_reached)\n            .max()\n            .unwrap_or(0);\n        below.saturating_add(u8::from(self.split_applied))\n    }\n\n    /// Every node that ended [`RecursiveExecution::Blocked`] with no children,\n    /// in execution order.\n    ///\n    /// These are the irreducible tasks: splitting could not shrink them and the\n    /// tool could not be extended for them, so they are precisely the places\n    /// where new capability has to be added.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn blocked_leaves(&self) -> Vec<&Self> {\n        if self.children.is_empty() {\n            return if self.is_passed() {\n                Vec::new()\n            } else {\n                vec![self]\n            };\n        }\n        self.children\n            .iter()\n            .flat_map(Self::blocked_leaves)\n            .collect()\n    }\n}\n\n/// How many times a failure may be split before the controller stops asking.\n///\n/// A splitter that keeps producing marginally different children would\n/// otherwise recurse without end. Four levels is more than the repository's own\n/// decomposition artifacts reach and still terminates in bounded work.\npub const DEFAULT_SPLIT_DEPTH_BOUND: u8 = 4;\n\n/// Execute the shrink-on-failure protocol over `root`.\n///\n/// Every node is attempted before descent. A failed branch executes its smaller\n/// children and is validated only if all of them pass. A failed node with no\n/// children is asked to split itself from its own failure; the children it\n/// yields are executed by this same protocol and the node is validated when\n/// they all pass. Only a node that cannot be split -- an irreducible task --\n/// gets one extension opportunity and one retry, which keeps execution bounded.\n///\n/// Splitting stops at [`DEFAULT_SPLIT_DEPTH_BOUND`]; use\n/// [`solve_recursively_within`] to choose another bound.\n#[must_use]\npub fn solve_recursively<E: TaskExecutor>(root: &RecursiveTask, executor: &mut E) -> RecursiveRun {\n    solve_recursively_within(root, executor, DEFAULT_SPLIT_DEPTH_BOUND)\n}\n\n/// [`solve_recursively`] with an explicit bound on failure-driven splitting.\n///\n/// A bound of zero reproduces the plan-driven protocol exactly: only the\n/// caller's tree is executed and a failed leaf goes straight to extension.\n#[must_use]\npub fn solve_recursively_within<E: TaskExecutor>(\n    root: &RecursiveTask,\n    executor: &mut E,\n    split_depth_bound: u8,\n) -> RecursiveRun {\n    execute(root, executor, 0, split_depth_bound)\n}\n\nfn execute<E: TaskExecutor>(\n    root: &RecursiveTask,\n    executor: &mut E,\n    split_depth: u8,\n    split_depth_bound: u8,\n) -> RecursiveRun {\n    let first = executor.attempt(root);\n    if first.passed {\n        return RecursiveRun {\n            task: root.clone(),\n            attempts: vec![first],\n            children: Vec::new(),\n            extension_applied: false,\n            split_applied: false,\n            status: RecursiveExecution::Passed,\n        };\n    }\n\n    let (supplied, split_applied) = if root.children.is_empty() {\n        let split = if split_depth < split_depth_bound {\n            usable_split(root, executor.split(root, &first, split_depth))\n        } else {\n            Vec::new()\n        };\n        let applied = !split.is_empty();\n        (split, applied)\n    } else {\n        (root.children.clone(), false)\n    };\n\n    if supplied.is_empty() {\n        let extension_applied = executor.extend_for(root, &first);\n        let mut attempts = vec![first];\n        if extension_applied {\n            attempts.push(executor.attempt(root));\n        }\n        let status = terminal_state(&attempts);\n        return RecursiveRun {\n            task: root.clone(),\n            attempts,\n            children: Vec::new(),\n            extension_applied,\n            split_applied: false,\n            status,\n        };\n    }\n\n    let child_depth = split_depth.saturating_add(u8::from(split_applied));\n    let children = supplied\n        .iter()\n        .map(|child| execute(child, executor, child_depth, split_depth_bound))\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n    let mut attempts = vec![first];\n    if children.iter().all(RecursiveRun::is_passed) {\n        attempts.push(executor.retry_after_children(root));\n    }\n    let status = terminal_state(&attempts);\n    RecursiveRun {\n        task: root.clone(),\n        attempts,\n        children,\n        extension_applied: false,\n        split_applied,\n        status,\n    }\n}\n\nfn terminal_state(attempts: &[TaskAttempt]) -> RecursiveExecution {\n    if attempts.last().is_some_and(|attempt| attempt.passed) {\n        RecursiveExecution::Passed\n    } else {\n        RecursiveExecution::Blocked\n    }\n}\n\n/// Drop split children that cannot shrink the problem.\n///\n/// A child that repeats its parent's identity or its goal would be attempted\n/// under the same conditions that just failed, so keeping it would trade a\n/// bounded protocol for an unbounded one. Discarding it makes the parent\n/// irreducible, which routes it to extension -- the honest outcome for a\n/// splitter that had nothing to say.\nfn usable_split(parent: &RecursiveTask, children: Vec<RecursiveTask>) -> Vec<RecursiveTask> {\n    children\n        .into_iter()\n        .filter(|child| child.id != parent.id && child.goal.trim() != parent.goal.trim())\n        .collect()\n}\n//! Incremental, failure-driven dispatch to external agentic CLIs.\n//!\n//! [`super::dispatch`]'s decompose mode splits the task once, up front, and\n//! sends every leaf out in parallel. That commits to a plan before any evidence\n//! exists: if a leaf turns out to be too large for the CLI, nothing splits it,\n//! and if the whole task was solvable as given, the split was wasted work.\n//!\n//! This mode inverts the order. The whole task is attempted first. Only a\n//! failure justifies a split, the pieces are executed by the same rule, and the\n//! parent is re-attempted once its pieces pass. The controller is\n//! [`crate::recursive_execution::solve_recursively`] and the splitter is\n//! [`crate::task_decomposition::SplittingExecutor`], so the shrink-on-failure\n//! protocol is the repository's own -- this module only supplies the tool\n//! boundary: an attempt is one recorded agent session in a copy of the\n//! workspace, and a passing attempt's effects are applied to the workspace\n//! before the next one starts.\n//!\n//! Extending the tool has a concrete meaning here. This controller cannot add a\n//! capability to somebody else's CLI, but it was given a list of CLIs; an\n//! irreducible task that one CLI failed is escalated to the next one that has\n//! not tried it. When the list is exhausted the task is reported blocked, with\n//! the evidence of every attempt, which is exactly the input the review-gated\n//! learning path needs.\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\n\nuse super::attribution::{commit_verified_effect, validate_effect_attribution};\nuse super::dispatch::{\n    ComparisonEntry, ComparisonLedger, DispatchConfig, DispatchError, DispatchMode, DispatchReport,\n    candidate_run_config, safe_name,\n};\nuse super::observe_orchestration_session;\nuse super::replay::write_session;\nuse super::runner::{AgentSession, run_agent, verify_workspace};\nuse super::workspace::{WorkspaceChange, apply_changes, copy_workspace};\nuse crate::client_contract_learning::learn_client_contracts;\nuse crate::links_format::push_lino_node;\nuse crate::recursive_execution::{\n    RecursiveRun, RecursiveTask, TaskAttempt, TaskExecutor, solve_recursively,\n};\nuse crate::task_decomposition::SplittingExecutor;\n\nconst COMPOSED_VERIFIER: &str = \"composed-verifier\";\n\n/// One attempted task, in execution order. The index into\n/// [`DispatchReport::sessions`] is this step's position in `steps`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct IncrementalStep {\n    /// Identity of the executed task node.\n    pub task_id: String,\n    /// The task text handed to the CLI.\n    pub task: String,\n    /// CLI that ran this attempt, or `composed-verifier` when the controller\n    /// accepted already-composed child effects without another agent call.\n    pub cli: String,\n    /// Whether the session and its verification passed.\n    pub passed: bool,\n    /// Recorded session file, relative to the output directory.\n    pub session_file: String,\n}\n\n/// One split the controller performed after a failure.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct IncrementalSplit {\n    /// The task that failed and was split.\n    pub task: String,\n    /// Evidence from the failing attempt that justified the split.\n    pub failure_evidence: String,\n    /// How many splits already happened above this task.\n    pub split_depth: u8,\n    /// Sub-tasks produced, in composition order. Empty means the splitter\n    /// declared the task irreducible.\n    pub children: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n/// A task no CLI in the list could solve, written out for review.\n///\n/// This is the run's own request to be extended: it names the task, every CLI\n/// that already tried it, and the evidence each attempt produced. Nothing here\n/// activates anything -- promotion stays behind the same review gate\n/// [`crate::task_decomposition::TaskStrategyLedger`] applies to a learned\n/// decomposition strategy.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct IncrementalProposal {\n    /// Stable identity of this proposal, from the task and its evidence.\n    pub id: String,\n    /// The irreducible task that stayed unsolved.\n    pub task: String,\n    /// Every CLI that attempted it, in the order they were tried.\n    pub tried_clis: Vec<String>,\n    /// Evidence from each failing attempt, in execution order.\n    pub failure_evidence: Vec<String>,\n    /// Always `human_review_required`: a run cannot approve its own extension.\n    pub status: String,\n}\n\nimpl IncrementalProposal {\n    /// This proposal as Links Notation, in the review-gated learning vocabulary.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn links_notation(&self) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::new();\n        push_lino_node(&mut out, 0, \"incremental_proposal\", Some(&self.id));\n        push_lino_node(&mut out, 2, \"task\", Some(&self.task));\n        for cli in &self.tried_clis {\n            push_lino_node(&mut out, 2, \"tried_cli\", Some(cli));\n        }\n        for evidence in &self.failure_evidence {\n            push_lino_node(&mut out, 2, \"failure_evidence\", Some(evidence));\n        }\n        push_lino_node(&mut out, 2, \"status\", Some(&self.status));\n        out\n    }\n}\n\n/// Everything the failure-driven run did, in the order it did it.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct IncrementalTrace {\n    /// Schema identity of this trace.\n    pub schema: String,\n    /// Whether the root task ended up passing.\n    pub solved: bool,\n    /// Deepest level of failure-driven splitting the run reached.\n    pub split_depth_reached: u8,\n    /// Every attempt, in execution order.\n    pub steps: Vec<IncrementalStep>,\n    /// Every split the controller requested.\n    pub splits: Vec<IncrementalSplit>,\n    /// Irreducible tasks that no CLI in the list could solve.\n    pub blocked_tasks: Vec<String>,\n    /// One review request per blocked task, mirrored to `proposals.lino`.\n    pub proposals: Vec<IncrementalProposal>,\n}\n\n/// Run one task incrementally and report every attempt, split, and effect.\npub(super) fn dispatch_incrementally(\n    config: &DispatchConfig,\n    workspace: &Path,\n    output_dir: &Path,\n) -> Result<DispatchReport, DispatchError> {\n    let root = RecursiveTask::leaf(root_id(&config.task), config.task.clone());\n    let mut executor = SplittingExecutor::new(AgentExecutor::new(config, workspace, output_dir));\n    let run = solve_recursively(&root, &mut executor);\n    let splits = executor\n        .splits()\n        .iter()\n        .map(|split| IncrementalSplit {\n            task: split.goal.clone(),\n            failure_evidence: split.failure_evidence.clone(),\n            split_depth: split.split_depth,\n            children: split.children.clone(),\n        })\n        .collect();\n    let agent = executor.into_inner();\n    if let Some(error) = agent.error {\n        return Err(error);\n    }\n    write_learning(output_dir, &agent.steps, &agent.sessions)?;\n\n    let entries = agent\n        .steps\n        .iter()\n        .zip(agent.sessions.iter())\n        .map(|(step, session)| ComparisonEntry {\n            cli: step.cli.clone(),\n            task: session.task.clone(),\n            passed: session.passed(),\n            diff_size: session.diff_size(),\n            wall_time_ms: session.wall_time_ms,\n            session_file: step.session_file.clone(),\n        })\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n    let proposals = proposals(&run, &agent.steps);\n    write_proposals(&config.output_dir, &proposals)?;\n    let trace = IncrementalTrace {\n        schema: \"formal-ai-incremental-trace-v1\".to_string(),\n        solved: run.is_passed(),\n        split_depth_reached: run.split_depth_reached(),\n        steps: agent.steps,\n        splits,\n        blocked_tasks: blocked_tasks(&run),\n        proposals,\n    };\n    Ok(DispatchReport {\n        schema: \"formal-ai-dispatch-report-v1\".to_string(),\n        mode: DispatchMode::Incremental,\n        tasks: trace.steps.iter().map(|step| step.task.clone()).collect(),\n        sessions: agent.sessions,\n        ledger: ComparisonLedger {\n            schema: \"formal-ai-comparison-ledger-v1\".to_string(),\n            selection_rule: \"pass,diff_size,wall_time,cli,session_file\".to_string(),\n            entries,\n            winner: None,\n        },\n        composed_changes: agent.changes,\n        incremental: Some(trace),\n    })\n}\n\n/// Feed the exact execution sessions into the existing proposal-only client\n/// contract learner. Incremental execution and auto-learning are one lifecycle:\n/// a run always preserves what it learned, while promotion remains a separate\n/// human decision enforced by the learner itself.\nfn write_learning(\n    output_dir: &Path,\n    steps: &[IncrementalStep],\n    sessions: &[AgentSession],\n) -> Result<(), DispatchError> {\n    let observations = steps\n        .iter()\n        .zip(sessions)\n        .filter(|(step, _)| step.cli != COMPOSED_VERIFIER)\n        .map(|(step, session)| observe_orchestration_session(session, &step.session_file))\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n    let learning = learn_client_contracts(&observations, &crate::seed::client_integrations());\n    std::fs::write(output_dir.join(\"learning.lino\"), learning.links_notation())\n        .map_err(DispatchError::Io)\n}\n\n/// Goals of the irreducible tasks a run could not solve, in execution order.\nfn blocked_tasks(run: &RecursiveRun) -> Vec<String> {\n    run.blocked_leaves()\n        .into_iter()\n        .map(|leaf| leaf.task.goal.clone())\n        .collect()\n}\n\nfn root_id(task: &str) -> String {\n    crate::engine::stable_id(\"dispatch_task\", task)\n}\n\n/// One review request per blocked task, in execution order.\n///\n/// A run that ends with something unsolved has produced the one thing the\n/// learning path cannot invent: a named task, the tools that were tried, and\n/// what each of them reported. Writing it out is what makes the next extension\n/// reviewable rather than guessed.\nfn proposals(run: &RecursiveRun, steps: &[IncrementalStep]) -> Vec<IncrementalProposal> {\n    run.blocked_leaves()\n        .into_iter()\n        .map(|leaf| {\n            let attempts = steps.iter().filter(|step| step.task_id == leaf.task.id);\n            let mut tried_clis: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n            for attempt in attempts {\n                if !tried_clis.contains(&attempt.cli) {\n                    tried_clis.push(attempt.cli.clone());\n                }\n            }\n            let failure_evidence: Vec<String> = leaf\n                .attempts\n                .iter()\n                .filter(|attempt| !attempt.passed)\n                .map(|attempt| attempt.evidence.clone())\n                .collect();\n            let id = crate::engine::stable_id(\n                \"incremental_proposal\",\n                &format!(\"{}|{}\", leaf.task.id, failure_evidence.join(\"|\")),\n            );\n            IncrementalProposal {\n                id,\n                task: leaf.task.goal.clone(),\n                tried_clis,\n                failure_evidence,\n                status: \"human_review_required\".to_string(),\n            }\n        })\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// Mirror the proposals next to the report, in the notation review reads.\n///\n/// A run with nothing blocked writes the file anyway, empty but for its header:\n/// \"no proposal\" and \"the run never got that far\" are different answers, and a\n/// missing file cannot tell them apart.\nfn write_proposals(\n    output_dir: &Path,\n    proposals: &[IncrementalProposal],\n) -> Result<(), DispatchError> {\n    let mut document = String::new();\n    push_lino_node(&mut document, 0, \"incremental_proposals\", None);\n    for proposal in proposals {\n        document.push_str(&proposal.links_notation());\n    }\n    std::fs::write(output_dir.join(\"proposals.lino\"), document).map_err(DispatchError::Io)\n}\n\n/// What an attempt observed, as the splitter and the reviewer read it.\n///\n/// Machine evidence, not prose: each field is one whitespace-free `key:value`\n/// token, so the record stays greppable and the split decision is made from\n/// facts a reader can check against the recorded session.\nfn evidence_of(cli: &str, session: &AgentSession) -> String {\n    let verification = session\n        .verification\n        .iter()\n        .map(|result| format!(\"{}={}\", result.program, result.passed))\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n        .join(\",\");\n    let exit = session\n        .exit_code\n        .map_or_else(|| \"none\".to_string(), |code| code.to_string());\n    [\n        format!(\"cli:{cli}\"),\n        format!(\"status:{:?}\", session.status),\n        format!(\"exit:{exit}\"),\n        format!(\"verification:{verification}\"),\n    ]\n    .join(\" \")\n}\n\n/// The tool boundary: one attempt is one recorded agent session.\nstruct AgentExecutor<'config> {\n    config: &'config DispatchConfig,\n    workspace: PathBuf,\n    output_dir: PathBuf,\n    sessions: Vec<AgentSession>,\n    steps: Vec<IncrementalStep>,\n    changes: Vec<WorkspaceChange>,\n    /// How many CLIs each task has already consumed, keyed by task identity.\n    escalations: BTreeMap<String, usize>,\n    /// The first controller error, kept because the executor trait has no way\n    /// to report one. A run that hit it is reported as an error, never as a\n    /// failed task: a controller fault is not evidence about the task.\n    error: Option<DispatchError>,\n}\n\nimpl<'config> AgentExecutor<'config> {\n    fn new(config: &'config DispatchConfig, workspace: &Path, output_dir: &Path) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            config,\n            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n            output_dir: output_dir.to_path_buf(),\n            sessions: Vec::new(),\n            steps: Vec::new(),\n            changes: Vec::new(),\n            escalations: BTreeMap::new(),\n            error: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Which CLI runs this task next: the first one, then one further along the\n    /// list for each escalation this task has been granted.\n    fn cli_for(&self, task: &RecursiveTask) -> String {\n        let index = self.escalations.get(&task.id).copied().unwrap_or(0);\n        self.config.clis[index.min(self.config.clis.len() - 1)].clone()\n    }\n\n    fn record(&mut self, error: DispatchError) {\n        if self.error.is_none() {\n            self.error = Some(error);\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn preserve_session(\n        &mut self,\n        task: &RecursiveTask,\n        cli: String,\n        session: AgentSession,\n    ) -> TaskAttempt {\n        let index = self.sessions.len();\n        let session_file = format!(\"sessions/{index:03}-{}.json\", safe_name(&cli));\n        if let Err(error) = write_session(&self.output_dir.join(&session_file), &session) {\n            self.record(DispatchError::Replay(error));\n            return TaskAttempt::failed(\"controller_aborted\");\n        }\n        self.record_preserved_session(task, cli, session, session_file)\n    }\n\n    fn record_preserved_session(\n        &mut self,\n        task: &RecursiveTask,\n        cli: String,\n        session: AgentSession,\n        session_file: String,\n    ) -> TaskAttempt {\n        let passed = session.passed();\n        let evidence = evidence_of(&cli, &session);\n        self.steps.push(IncrementalStep {\n            task_id: task.id.clone(),\n A separate non-mutating minimum qualifying-PR simulation at the preceding head projected a three-release share of only 0.90% against the required non-decreasing 12.77% target. No release gate or attribution check is bypassed here.
